title: Savannah Guthrie delivers 'very specific' message to mom's kidnapper 25 weeks after her abduction
summary: Savannah Guthrie posted an emotional Instagram plea with a "very specific" message directed at whoever kidnapped her mother, Nancy Guthrie.
story: Savannah Guthrie issued a new plea on Instagram to those who kidnapped her mother, Nancy Guthrie, in a video posted July 27, 2026. (Credit: @savannahguthrie/Instagram)
Savannah Guthrie delivered a "very specific" message to her mother's kidnapper on Monday, more than 25 weeks after the 84-year-old Nancy Guthrie vanished from her Arizona home.

In an emotional plea posted to her Instagram account, Savannah Guthrie appealed directly to whoever is responsible for the kidnapping, saying that her family is "in agony" and "will never stop looking for her."
"Do the right thing now," Guthrie urged her mother's unidentified kidnappers. "Make the right choice. Help us find her. Tell us where to look for her."
NANCY GUTHRIE UPDATE: 25 WEEKS AFTER ABDUCTION, ELIZABETH SMART SAYS THERE'S ‘REASON TO HAVE HOPE’
An undated photo of Nancy Guthrie and Savannah Guthrie, provided by NBC in response to the disappearance of the 84-year-old mother of the 'Today' host. (Courtesy of NBC)

"I'm coming on today with a very specific message. It has been months since our mom was taken from us. Our family is in agony. We are in a nightmare that will not end. Nothing about our situation has changed. We have done our part, and we will never stop looking for her. We will always ache for her and feel that hole in our hearts. The world can be a cruel and unforgiving place," Savannah Guthrie said. "I truly believe it is never too late to do right thing. Help us bring this situation to an end. For all of us. No matter where we've been and what we've done, I believe there is always a way home. Please make the right choice."
The new message is her first in weeks, as official updates have slowed to a trickle and there have been no signs of her mother's whereabouts.
NANCY GUTHRIE'S SUSPECTED ABDUCTION: TIMELINE OF EVENTS IN DISAPPEARANCE OF ‘TODAY’ HOST'S MOM

Savannah Guthrie and her husband, Michael Feldman, were seen arriving at LaGuardia Airport in New York City on the morning of July 17 as the couple prepared to head out of town. Guthrie had just wrapped up hosting her portion of the "Today" broadcast and had walked off the set a day earlier, when an intruder breached security and accosted colleague Craig Melvin. She has been off-air since filming a new "Wordle" game show. (T. Jackson/Backgrid)
The family is asking anyone with information to dial 1-800-CALL-FBI and claim a reward of over $1 million.

There is also a separate reward for information that leads to an arrest that can be obtained anonymously by calling 520-88-CRIME, Tucson's Crime Stoppers affiliate.
The elder Guthrie, 84, was taken from her home in Tucson's Catalina Foothills neighborhood in the early hours of Feb. 1, according to the Pima County Sheriff's Department.

The results of DNA testing and other forensics have not been made public as the case drags on without signs of Guthrie. A purported ransom note and an apparent follow-up message that claimed she had died have not been confirmed as authentic by investigators.

title: Former college soccer player found dead off San Diego beach in one of nation's wealthiest beach communities
summary: Bryn Waite, a former Central Washington University soccer player from Anchorage, was found dead in waters off La Jolla Shores Beach in San Diego.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.
A former college soccer player has been identified as the 26-year-old woman found dead in the waters off San Diego's La Jolla Shores Beach as investigators work to determine what happened.

title: Bryan Kohberger waived his appeal rights but plans on pursuing post-conviction relief: sources
summary: Bryan Kohberger plans to file for post-conviction relief after pleading guilty to killing four University of Idaho students, two sources say.
story: The longtime attorney and true crime host says prosecutors had a "slam dunk" case against Bryan Kohberger, which led to the plea deal — dismissing his defense claims of shaky evidence against the convicted killer.

The admitted murderer Bryan Kohberger plans to file for post-conviction relief after pleading guilty to killing four University of Idaho students in a 4 a.m. home invasion attack, according to two sources familiar with the matter.
Kohberger plans to argue that he had bad counsel. Court records show he filed a petition for post-conviction relief Monday, but the filing itself was not immediately available.

Kohberger, in his handwritten petition, claims that he was "convinced to falsely confess," claiming his high-profile defense team of Anne Taylor, Elisa Massoth and Bicka Barlow didn't tell him about "exculpatory discovery" — evidence mentioned in the recent "Broken Plea" book but never vetted in court.

The New York Times was first to report this story after Kohberger called a reporter directly and claimed that he has an "absolute claim of innocence" in his first public remarks outside the courtroom.
IDAHO MURDERS EVIDENCE LEAK TRIGGERS CRIMINAL INVESTIGATION FOR INSIDER WHO SPILLED SECRETS: REPORT

Bryan Kohberger appears at the Ada County Courthouse in Boise, Idaho, on July 23, 2025, for sentencing in the University of Idaho murders case, where prosecutors relied heavily on cellphone location data and digital evidence. (Photo by Kyle Green-Pool/Getty Images)
"My actual innocence is my truth, and the plea, hinged on by false promises and blatant disinformation, MUST be withdrawn," he told the outlet.

The family of victim Kaylee Goncalves ripped into Kohberger and his supporters as "the mosquito you just can't seem to swat." Kohberger's petition fails to acknowledge that he told Idaho Judge Steven Hippler last year that he "knowingly, voluntarily and intelligently" admitted to the crime in court, the family said in a statement.

"Quite the opposite," the statement continued. "He appeared in court for a hearing before a judge, accompanied by his four lawyers. He chose not to leave his fate—or the facts of the case—to a jury. He never cried foul, never claimed he was uninformed or pressured, and never suggested there were problems with the discovery materials he and his counsel had reviewed for two years that should have been challenged. He admitted his guilt. When asked whether he was actually guilty, he answered, 'Yes.'"
LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST
The family would have preferred the case go to trial with the death penalty still on the table.
"Instead, BK received exactly what he asked for: a deal that spared his life," the family said. "Know this—he hates that life."
Kohberger has repeatedly complained about prison conditions as he sits in isolation at the Idaho Maximum Security Institute.
Idaho Attorney General Raúl Labrador told Fox News Digital his office is "ready to do whatever is necessary to ensure justice is fully carried out."
"My heart goes out to the families of Madison, Kaylee, Xana, and Ethan, who have already endured unimaginable loss and now must face today’s deeply painful news," he said.

Madison Mogen, top left, smiles on the shoulders of her best friend, Kaylee Goncalves, as they pose with Ethan Chapin, Xana Kernodle, and two other housemates in Goncalves' final Instagram post, shared the day before the four students were stabbed to death. (@kayleegoncalves/Instagram)

Labrador's office assisted Latah County prosecutors in defeating virtually all of Kohberger's pretrial motions seeking to suppress evidence in the case, which resulted in his guilty plea weeks before he would have gone to trial and faced the potential death penalty if convicted.
In his message to the Times, Kohberger claimed that "justice was not served" and that it was "circumnavigated by a broken plea."

"Broken Plea" is the title of a recent book about the case that shed new light on what the defense may have looked like at trial — and his use of the term surprised author Chris Whitcomb, who says he had never spoken to Kohberger.
"He would have to show ‘manifest injustice,’" said Joshua Ritter, a California-based defense attorney and Fox News contributor. "Essentially his lawyers lied to him."

A watchman parked outside 1122 King Road on Dec. 11, 2022, four weeks after four students were stabbed to death inside. A year later, the property is scheduled for demolition. Critics believe it should remain standing until the suspect goes to trial.  (Michael Ruiz/Fox News Digital)
One hypothesis floated in Whitcomb's book is that Kohberger may not have fully understood or meaningfully participated in the decision to plead guilty.
FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X

Kohberger is serving four consecutive life sentences with no possibility of parole plus another 10 years for the Nov. 13, 2022 murders of Xana Kernodle, Ethan Chapin, Madison Mogen and Kaylee Goncalves after pleading guilty in July 2025.

Police found his DNA on a knife sheath in a bed with two of the four victims, Mogen and Goncalves. They also tracked his vehicle coming and going, and forensic investigators were prepared to testify about how although he shut his phone off during the murders, the evidence suggested he drove to and from the crime scene anyway.

As part of the plea deal, he waived his right to an appeal — and Monday's filing caught some of the victims' relatives by surprise.
"I didn't think he could do that, since that was part of the stipulation in the first place — he wasn't going to be able to do that," said Cara Northington, Kernodle's mother.
This is a breaking news story. Stick with Fox News Digital for updates.

title: Lindsay Clancy ‘deliberately and meticulously killed’ her 3 children, prosecutor tells jury
summary: Lindsay Clancy's defense claims postpartum psychosis drove her to strangle her three children, while prosecutors allege the killings were planned.
story: Lindsay Clancy appeared to become emotional as prosecutors introduced jurors to Cora, Dawson and Callan during opening statements in the Massachusetts mother's murder trial.
This story discusses suicide. If you or someone you know is having thoughts of suicide, please contact the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline at 988 or 1-800-273-TALK (8255).
Patrick Clancy took the stand Monday and described watching his wife fall into a "big spiral" before she allegedly strangled their three young children inside the family’s Massachusetts home.

Testifying as the first witness in Lindsay Clancy’s murder trial, Patrick said his then-wife lost weight, became severely depressed and began expressing suicidal thoughts after she was prescribed Seroquel.

"Awful," Patrick said when asked how she was doing physically after beginning the medication. "That was really where her big spiral started. She started to lose a lot of weight, and she became very depressed, and she was having a really hard time."
LINDSAY CLANCY’S HUSBAND COULD TESTIFY FOR HER AT TRIAL OVER DEATHS OF THEIR THREE CHILDREN
Lindsay Clancy reacts as the details of her children's deaths are read in court on Monday. (Greg Derr/Pool/The Patriot Ledger)

Patrick testified that Lindsay later told him she was suicidal, although she denied having a plan to kill herself. He said she also described experiencing intrusive thoughts about harming their children.
"I never saw Lindsay harm the kids," he testified.

Patrick Clancy took the stand around 11:45 a.m. as the first witness in the trial. Patrick and Lindsay Clancy were married at the time their three children were killed in the couple's Duxbury, Massachusetts home. They have since divorced and Patrick is remarried.  (Pool)

His testimony came after prosecutors and defense attorneys offered starkly different accounts of the deaths of Cora, 5, Dawson, 3, and Callan, 8 months, during opening statements in Plymouth Superior Court.
Prosecutor Shanan Buckingham told jurors that the children were "deliberately and meticulously killed" by their mother on Jan. 24, 2023.
"They were strangled — deliberately and meticulously killed by this defendant," Buckingham said shortly after beginning the prosecution’s opening statement.
Buckingham urged the panel of 12 women and six men to keep an open mind, use their common sense and weigh the evidence presented during the trial.
Defense attorney Kevin Reddington countered that Clancy deeply loved and cared for her children and did not kill them because she viewed them as an impediment to her life.

"These children were loved and nurtured and cared for by her," Reddington told jurors. "She didn’t want to get rid of her kids because of her selfish life. As the government indicates, she loved those children right up to the time of their death."

Clancy, a former labor and delivery nurse at Massachusetts General Hospital, has pleaded not guilty to three counts each of murder and strangulation. Her attorneys contend she was suffering from severe postpartum psychosis and was not criminally responsible for her actions.

Lindsay Clancy was indicted on three counts each of murder in the 2023 deaths of her 5-year-old daughter Cora, 3-year-old son Dawson and 7-month-old son Callan. She pleaded not guilty to the charges. (Greg Derr/The Patriot Ledger via Pool)

Patrick testified that he and Lindsay met in 2013 and later began dating. He said she experienced anxiety after each of their children’s births, particularly as the end of her maternity leave approached.
He recalled Lindsay telling him that she planned to begin taking Zoloft because she believed it would help with her anxiety and her return to work.
"She said, ‘I think it’s really going to help with my anxiety and with going back to work,’" Patrick testified.
When he asked how she planned to obtain the prescription, Patrick recalled her saying, "Usually you just ask the doctor, and they’ll give it to you."

Patrick also said he became concerned after Lindsay was prescribed 10 medications in slightly more than two months. He pushed for her to receive an in-person medical evaluation because many of her telehealth appointments appeared brief and lacked sufficient attention, he testified.
"I felt like it had to be in person because I just felt like there was a disconnect," Patrick said.
Plymouth County Assistant District Attorney Shanan Buckingham delivers her opening statement in court on Monday.  (Greg Derr/Pool/The Patriot Ledger)

Her attorneys do not dispute that she killed the children but plan to argue that she was experiencing postpartum psychosis and lacked criminal responsibility. Prosecutors allege the killings were intentional and carefully planned.

"It is usually a hard battle to win," criminal defense attorney and Fox News contributor Donna Rotunno told Fox News Digital of the defense's insanity bid. "But given the fact that she has such a documented history of treatment and going to doctors and being diagnosed and seeking out more treatment when she wasn’t doing well, I think she can lay the groundwork for it."
Rotunno said Clancy’s attorneys are likely to emphasize that her condition allegedly continued to deteriorate even as she sought medical help.

"She continued to get worse. She continued to seek treatment," Rotunno said, pointing to reports that Clancy discussed hearing voices and was prescribed several medications before the children’s deaths.

Clancy’s prior work as a nurse could cut both ways at trial. Prosecutors may argue that her medical background made her more capable of understanding her treatment and actions, but Rotunno said the defense could use the same fact to demonstrate the severity of her alleged psychosis.
"She was a nurse and still so out of it that she didn’t know she shouldn’t be taking all this stuff," Rotunno said. "That, to me, doesn’t play into the intention on this. It’s the total opposite."
Lindsay Clancy with two of her three children in this undated photo. (Lindsay Marie Clancy/ Facebook)
Authorities said Patrick Clancy left the family’s Duxbury home on Jan. 24, 2023, to pick up takeout food and an item from a pharmacy.
While he was gone, prosecutors allege, Lindsay Clancy used exercise bands to strangle the children before jumping from a second-story window in an apparent suicide attempt.
FLORIDA AG SEEKS JUDGE'S IMPEACHMENT AFTER BABY DROWNING COVID INSANITY ACQUITTAL
The fall left her paralyzed, and she now uses a wheelchair.

Cora and Dawson were pronounced dead after being taken to a Plymouth hospital. Callan was flown to Boston Children’s Hospital and died several days later. The medical examiner determined that Cora and Dawson died from asphyxia and that Callan died from complications of asphyxia.

Exterior view of the home of Patrick and Lindsay Clancy in Duxbury, MA on Wednesday, Feb. 15, 2023. Lindsay Clancy, 32, allegedly killed their three children here before attempting to take her own life on Jan. 24, 2023. (David McGlynn for Fox News Digital)
Clancy’s mental condition in the months and weeks before the killings are expected to become the central battleground at trial.
LUIGI MANGIONE OVERRULED HIS OWN LAWYERS WITH A 'CHANGE OF HEART' ON PSYCH DEFENSE, LEGAL EXPERT SAYS
Her attorneys say she sought help repeatedly as she struggled with depression, sleeplessness, suicidal thoughts and voices urging her to harm herself and the children.
If you or someone you know is having thoughts of suicide, please contact the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline at 1-800-273-TALK (8255).
If you or someone you know is having thoughts of suicide, please contact the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline at 1-800-273-TALK (8255).
She was admitted to a psychiatric hospital weeks before the deaths and was prescribed several medications as providers attempted to treat her worsening symptoms.

According to lawsuits filed by Lindsay and Patrick Clancy against her medical providers, she heard a voice on the day of the killings telling her it was her "last chance" to kill the children and herself.
The lawsuits accuse her providers of failing to properly diagnose, treat and monitor a severe postpartum psychiatric condition.
The defense is expected to argue Clancy lacks criminal responsibility because she suffered from postpartum psychosis and was overmedicated. (Greg Derr/The Patriot Ledger via Pool)

Plymouth Superior Court Judge William Sullivan ruled Friday that the media and public may not record, display, reproduce or distribute Patrick Clancy’s initial 911 call or autopsy photographs of the children.
The ruling came after Patrick requested that the evidence be shielded by media dissemination.
Reporters may also describe what is heard or shown in court but cannot broadcast or publish the recording or images themselves, according to the two-page order.
Exterior view of the home of Patrick and Lindsay Clancy in Duxbury, Massachusetts, on Wednesday, Feb. 15, 2023. (David McGlynn for Fox News Digital)
The privacy dispute produced a heated courtroom exchange Thursday after the jury was seated.

Patrick Clancy asked Sullivan to limit the public and media’s ability to record, broadcast or distribute his initial 911 call, family and crime-scene photographs of the children, autopsy images and the clothing the children were wearing.
FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X

His attorney, David Meier, said the request was not intended to close the courtroom, prevent jurors from seeing the evidence or interfere with either side’s case. Instead, he argued that allowing the materials to circulate online would cause lasting emotional harm to Patrick Clancy.
SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS
Lindsay Clancy's murder trial is expected to last six to eight weeks, and the witness list contains more than 200 names. (Greg Derr/The Patriot Ledger via Pool)
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE
Reddington supported Patrick’s request and accused prosecutors of planning to present the evidence in a manner designed to "inflame" the jury.
"Even though we’re in a court, let’s talk a little bit about humanity," Reddington said. "Let’s talk a little bit about how we should try this case."
SEND US A TIP
Reddington said Patrick had suffered "one of the worst tragedies that anyone could ever suffer" and was attempting to rebuild his life.

"How that guy is still not an emotional basket case is beyond me. But nevertheless, he is trying hard to move on with his life. He has, as the court is aware, divorced. He’s remarried. He has a family. He has his extended family," he said.
Lindsay and Patrick Clancy with two of their three children in this undated photo. (Lindsay Marie Clancy/ Facebook)
GOT A TIP?
Reddington accused the prosecution of trying "to put a circus in front of this jury" and later called its approach "reprehensible."
"The district attorney wants to put that guy on the witness stand and show little onesies with bodily fluid of his child?" he said.

Superior Court Judge William Sullivan presides over day three of jury selection Wednesday, July 22, 2026, in the triple murder trial of Lindsay Clancy, who is accused of murdering her three young children in 2023 in their Duxbury, Massachusetts home. (Greg Derr/The Patriot Ledger via Pool)

title: 15-year-old arrested after Seattle Center mass shooting leaves 3 dead, 4 wounded
summary: A 15-year-old was detained as Seattle police searched for a second suspect after gunfire outside the Seattle Center Armory killed three people and wounded four others.
story: Three people were killed and multiple others were wounded on Sunday in a mass shooting incident in Seattle, police said. (KCPQ)

A 15-year-old was taken into custody as police continue to search for a second suspect after three people were killed, and four others were wounded Sunday in a mass shooting at the Seattle Center, according to Mayor Katie Wilson and police.
"We believe this teenager opened fire in the crowd, but details are still under investigation," Wilson said.

No homicide charges have been filed against the teen, who was booked into juvenile detention on suspicion of firearms violations and first-degree assault, Wilson said. The juvenile was expected to make an initial court appearance Monday.
Seattle Police Department Chief Shon Barnes said investigators believe two individuals exchanged gunfire outside the Seattle Center Armory, leaving multiple bystanders caught in the crossfire.
MULTIPLE INJURED AFTER FLOATPLANE MAKES EMERGENCY LANDING, CATCHES FIRE OFF WASHINGTON COAST
Seattle Police urged people to avoid the area. (KCPQ)
Police believe the shooting stemmed from a conflict between two small groups who appear to be at odds with each other.

An active manhunt remains underway for the second suspected shooter. However, police acknowledged it is technically possible that one of the fatally shot victims was the second gunman, though that has not been confirmed.
Officials said a 19-year-old man and a 44-year-old man died at the scene despite life-saving efforts by first responders.
A 56-year-old woman was also transported to a local hospital in critical condition, where she later died.

Four other victims were injured, including a 2-year-old boy, a 23-year-old man, a 39-year-old woman and a 40-year-old woman. Officials said the toddler, who was initially transported to the hospital in stable condition, has since been upgraded to satisfactory condition. The remaining victims either suffered minor injuries or had already been discharged from the hospital.
Police are also investigating whether a 27-year-old man who self-transported to a hospital was an eighth victim. His involvement has not yet been confirmed.
Harborview Medical Center spokesperson Susan Gregg previously said the injuries to four patients involved an arm, abdomen and legs.
Wilson called the shooting "an act of horrific violence."

"Impacted families are living through the worst moment of their lives, and an entire community is trying to understand how a gathering built around culture, connection, and joy ended in gunfire," Wilson said in a statement. "No one should have to weigh the risk of being shot before attending an event, gathering with friends, or experiencing their city."
The venue was hosting the Bite of Seattle food festival over the weekend.
"Our first responsibilities are supporting grieving families, caring for the injured, and providing clear and accurate information for the public," the mayor said.
Washington Gov. Bob Ferguson previously said he was receiving briefings and State Patrol SWAT officers responded to the scene to assist Seattle Police.
"My prayers are with the families of the victims, and the responders as they work to keep people safe," the governor said on X.
Police and emergency crews began arriving at Seattle Center shortly after 6 p.m. The venue was hosting the Bite of Seattle food festival over the weekend. (KCPQ)
Fox News Digital reached out to the Seattle Police Department for additional information.
Rep. Pramila Jayapal, D-Wash., said she was "absolutely horrified" by the shooting.
"My heart goes out to the victims and their families, and all those impacted by this senseless violence."

"I am grateful to the officers and first responders who are at the scene and working to protect our community, as well as the frontline medical professionals who are treating survivors," she said on X. "Tonight, we grieve with our community in Seattle as well as those around the country affected by gun violence and mass shootings."
King County Executive Girmay Zahilay similarly said he was "horrified" by the violence.

"As someone who grew up in this community, I know what this event means to so many families, young people, and neighbors across our region," he said in a statement. "For years, the Bite has been one of Seattle's signature summer traditions. To see violence at a place that brings so many people together is heartbreaking and unacceptable."
Kayla Carris, 22, said she was sitting outside the Armory at the Bite of Seattle when people began to scream and run for cover inside the Seattle Center Armory.
SEATTLE FIRE CREWS RESPOND TO 3-ALARM INDUSTRIAL DISTRICT WAREHOUSE FIRE, ROOF PARTIALLY COLLAPSES
Three people were pronounced dead at the scene. (KCPQ)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
"Everyone was just throwing stuff and running," Carris told The Seattle Times. "Like everyone."
Todd Behrends, 59, said he heard what appeared to be several rounds of shots.
People began running and jumping over each other to escape, Behrends told the outlet. One woman fell, and someone stepped on her leg.
Behrends said he saw a woman on the ground and a man on a stretcher as he ran toward an exit.

title: Newborn vanished after secret birth, parents allegedly claimed baby 'was a prank': cops
summary: The Florida couple allegedly claimed their newborn was "a prank" after the baby vanished, but investigators developed evidence for manslaughter charges.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.
A Florida couple accused of claiming their missing infant never existed has been arrested in North Carolina after a yearlong investigation into the child’s presumed death.

Leon Alejandro Jr., 21, and Samantha Feliz, 20, both of Hollywood, Florida, were arrested Wednesday in Rockingham, North Carolina, where investigators say they fled while Hollywood police investigated the disappearance of their infant.

The pair were taken into custody by investigators with the Richmond County Sheriff's Office and the U.S. Marshals Service and booked into the Richmond County Jail on fugitive of justice warrants. They are being held without bond pending extradition to Florida.

Hollywood police began investigating the case in early 2025 after learning Feliz allegedly gave birth sometime between Dec. 6, 2024, and Jan. 5, 2025, according to the Richmond County Sheriff's Office.
DNA FROM SODA BOTTLE ALLEGEDLY LINKS MASSACHUSETTS WOMAN TO 1985 MURDER OF 'BABY BOY DOE'

Leon Alejandro Jr., 21, and Samantha Angeline Feliz, 20, were arrested in North Carolina and are awaiting extradition to Florida on multiple felony charges related to the disappearance of their infant. (Richmond County Sheriff's Office - N.C. via Facebook)
Authorities said the birth was concealed and happened somewhere other than a hospital.
Investigators said family members saw the couple with the baby during the child's first month of life. After that, authorities said, the infant was never seen again.

According to an arrest warrant obtained by WPLG, investigators believe the child, identified only by the initials A.F., was last photographed on Jan. 5, 2025. Detectives wrote that the infant appeared "visibly ill and malnourished" and showed "no signs of life" in what they described as the final known image.
The warrant also alleges investigators searched multiple locations with cadaver dogs but were unable to locate the child's remains, according to the outlet.
MAN ACCUSED OF KILLING PARTNER ARRESTED IN MEXICO NEARLY TWO YEARS AFTER FLEEING WITH THEIR TWO CHILDREN

Investigators with the Richmond County Sheriff's Office and the U.S. Marshals Service arrested the Florida couple at a property near Rockingham, North Carolina. (Richmond County Sheriff's Office - N.C. Facebook)

Authorities allege Alejandro and Feliz repeatedly denied the child existed, telling relatives the baby "was a prank" and later claiming the pregnancy had been a "hoax" intended to scam family members out of money, WPLG reported, citing the arrest warrant.
According to the outlet, investigators said photographs showed Feliz visibly pregnant, while text messages discussed the pregnancy and the baby.

Detectives also reportedly recovered baby clothing, a positive pregnancy test and what appeared to be blood-stained towels from a storage unit tied to the couple. DNA testing later determined blood recovered from the baby clothing and towels belonged to a biological child of Alejandro and Feliz, according to the warrant.

Despite the lack of a birth certificate or medical records, investigators said they developed enough evidence to charge both suspects with aggravated manslaughter of a child, tampering with or fabricating physical evidence, failure to report a death to the medical examiner, providing false information concerning a missing child and making false reports to law enforcement.
Authorities allege the couple fled Florida and were living on property belonging to one of Alejandro's relatives in Richmond County when investigators located and arrested them July 22.
'AMERICA'S MOST WANTED' FUGITIVE CAPTURED ON SAILBOAT OFF NJ COAST AFTER 20 YEARS ON THE RUN
Hollywood, Florida, lies on the Florida beach between Fort Lauderdale and Miami, and was named after the showbiz town in California. (fotog via Getty Images)
Richmond County Sheriff Mark Gulledge praised the multi-agency effort that led to the arrests.
"This is a prime example of agencies nationwide collaborating to uphold justice," Gulledge said in a statement.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Authorities have not publicly released additional details about what investigators believe happened to the infant.
Fox News Digital has reached out to the Richmond County Sheriff's Office for any additional updates on the investigation, but did not immediately receive a response.

title: NY circus performer airlifted to hospital after colleague's arrow misses target, strikes his neck
summary: A circus performer was airlifted to a hospital after his colleague's arrow struck his neck during a stunt at the Orange County Fair in Wallkill, police said.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.
A circus performer was airlifted to a hospital after his colleague missed her target and hit him in the neck with an arrow while performing in New York, according to authorities.

The incident happened as Edwin Cuervo Rangel, 38, and Ana Daza Tavera, 42, were performing at the Orange County Fair in the town of Wallkill at around 9:30 p.m. on Friday, New York State Police said in a press release.
Cuervo Rangel and Daza Tavera are married, according to News 12.
The two performers from Wisconsin were doing a stunt when Daza Tavera shot an arrow at a foam target that Cuervo Rangel was holding, according to police.
TOURIST DIES AT LUXURY RESORT AFTER COBRA FROM SNAKE SHOW CLIMBS UP PANTS, BITES HIM: POLICE
A circus performer was airlifted to a hospital after his wife and colleague missed her target and hit him in the neck with an arrow. (Orange County Fair/Facebook)
The arrow struck and injured Cuervo Rangel, police said.
Cuervo Rangel was airlifted to Westchester Medical Center in stable condition.
No other injuries were reported.
A ringmaster for the traveling show company, Circus Murcia, later said the arrow hit Cuervo Rangel in his neck.
"Well, last night, unfortunately, when she shot the crossbow, it caught him in his neck," Circus Murcia Ringmaster Benjamin Jackson told News 12.
LOUISIANA WOMAN HOSPITALIZED AFTER ROPE SWING MISHAP ON CRUISE EXCURSION LEFT HER WITH GENITAL TRAUMA
Edwin Cuervo Rangel was airlifted to a hospital in stable condition. (Orange County Fair/Facebook)
"The good news is, she caught him right at the very corner of the neck. There was no blood, nothing," he added.
Circus Murcia owner Alexander Murcia said Cuervo Rangel is expected to make a full recovery.

"Our thoughts remain with him during his recovery, and we sincerely appreciate the outstanding care provided by the first responders, medical team, and everyone who assisted," Murcia told the Hudson Valley Post.
Fox News Digital reached out to Circus Murcia for comment.
Edwin Cuervo Rangel is expected to make a full recovery. (Orange County Fair/Facebook)

The Orange County Fair opened on Thursday and is scheduled to be open daily through Aug. 2.

The Big Top Circus featuring Circus Murcia is new to the fair this year, featuring "breathtaking acrobatics, daring aerial performances, and world-class circus artistry," according to the fair's website.

title: Nevada man dies at famed Sequoia National Park trail after sudden emergency
summary: An elderly Nevada hiker died after a suffering from a medical emergency on a popular hiking trail in Sequoia National Park on Thursday.
story: A bull bison attacks camper at Yellowstone National Park. (Credit NewsFlare)
An elderly man reportedly died Thursday after suffering a medical emergency on a popular hiking trail in California's Sequoia National Park.
The victim was identified as 79-year-old John Francis Oliver of Henderson, Nevada, a suburb of Las Vegas, the Tulare County Sheriff's Office said, according to Your Central Valley.

Oliver was found along the General Sherman Tree Trail, a one-mile path that leads to the world's largest living tree, the General Sherman Tree, according to the outlet, citing the National Park Service (NPS).
First responders rendered emergency medical aid to Oliver at the scene, but the man was eventually pronounced dead in the park, according to SFGATE.
CAUSE OF DEATH REVEALED FOR BIG SUR HIKER WHOSE BODY WAS FOUND NAKED ON REMOTE CALIFORNIA TRAIL
The General Sherman giant sequoia tree stands in the Giant Forest in Sequoia National Park near Three Rivers, Calif., on October 22, 2021. (Patrick T. Fallon/AFP via Getty Images)

The Tulare County Sheriff's Office declined to release additional details about what led to the medical emergency or the circumstances surrounding Oliver's death "out of respect for the family," SFGATE reported.
The man’s cause of death has also not yet been determined.
PARK VISITORS FACE FLOOD DANGER OUT WEST WHILE SEVERE STORMS RIP THROUGH NY, NJ
Sequoia National Park, home to Giant Forest and Mount Whitney, hosts the largest tree in the world.  (iStock)
The incident came as temperatures in the region climbed into the upper 90s, according to the National Weather Service.
An extreme heat warning was also in effect Thursday for portions of the nearby Mojave Desert and Indian Wells Valley.
Thursday's death marks the latest in a string of fatal incidents at Sequoia National Park and nearby areas in recent months.
LONE SURVIVOR RESCUED AFTER FATAL FALL KILLS THREE CLIMBERS ON MOUNT MCKINLEY

In neighboring Kings Canyon National Park, a San Mateo couple drowned at Roaring River Falls in May, according to Fox 2 San Francisco.

title: Search intensifies for North Carolina physical therapist who vanished during Caribbean getaway
summary: Authorities are searching for missing North Carolina physical therapist Elizabeth Waddell after she vanished during a vacation in Grenada near Grand Anse Beach.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.
A North Carolina woman has vanished while on a trip to the Caribbean island of Grenada, sparking an urgent search as her family, friends and loved ones plead for her safe return.
Elizabeth "Liz" Waddell, 44, was last seen Wednesday at Grand Anse Beach in St. George's, near where she was staying in the Grand Anse area, according to the Royal Grenada Police Force.

Waddell, a physical therapist, wife and mother from the Raleigh area, is described as 5 feet 5 inches tall with short blonde hair. Authorities also released a photo showing Waddell with pink hair as they asked the public for help locating her.
According to her professional website, Waddell is the founder of Art of Movement Physical Therapy and earned a doctorate in physical therapy from the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill.
SEARCH UNDERWAY FOR AUSTRALIAN WOMAN WHO VANISHED AFTER SENDING MESSAGE ABOUT GOING FOR A HIKE NEAR LAS VEGAS
Liz Waddell smiles during a meal in an undated photo. (Cailen Waddell)
According to a friend who said she has known Waddell and her husband for more than 20 years, Waddell traveled to Grenada for a vacation with another friend, WRAL News reported.
Waddell's friend reportedly lost sight of her after remaining at their Airbnb to take an online course while Waddell went outside, apparently for a swim.

"She had her swimsuit on, and she went outside their Airbnb," Amanda Romano-Harmon said, according to the local outlet. "They had a pool that overlooked the bay. Liz was set up out there just sightseeing from the pool, and her friend was taking her online course. When she got through with her course, she looked up and she didn't see Liz outside, so she went outside to walk around and see where she went, and she saw her towel down on the pier. So the only thing we can think is maybe she went for a swim."
The friend reportedly became increasingly concerned over the next several hours, knowing Waddell did not have her phone with her, and eventually filed a missing-persons report.
THREE SISTERS FOUND DEAD IN OCEAN AT POPULAR TOURIST BEACH AS POLICE PROBE MYSTERIOUS TRAGEDY
Liz Waddell and her husband, Cailen, pose together for a photo during a trip.  (Cailen Waddell)
Waddell's husband, Cailen, was at work when he received the call about his wife's disappearance, according to the report.
He said on social media Friday that he was heading to the area to assist in the search and urged anyone with connections to the island to share information that could help locate her.
He also described Waddell as a kind-hearted person while speaking with local Grenada media outlets.
"My wife is a loving, free-spirited person. She could make friends with anyone. She often did," he told Grenada Broadcasting Network (GBN).

Police are urging anyone with information about Waddell's whereabouts to come forward, specifically asking fishermen, boat operators and residents along Grenada's southern coastline to report any sightings that could assist in the search.
KENTUCKY MAN CHARGED WITH BOATING UNDER THE INFLUENCE AFTER FEMALE PASSENGER, 19, GOES MISSING
Grenada officials issued a missing persons alert for Liz Waddell on July 23, 2026. (Royal Grenada Police Force)
According to GBN, an extensive search effort is underway with the assistance of police officers, divers and students from St. George's University.

The U.S. State Department told Fox News Digital on Sunday that officials are aware of reports of a missing American citizen in Grenada and emphasized that the Trump Administration has no higher priority than the safety and security of U.S. citizens abroad.

The State Department declined to provide additional details due to privacy considerations but said it can assist families and friends with filing missing persons reports and help them understand local procedures.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Aradia Fitness, where Waddell also works as a fitness instructor,  called the news of her disappearance "disheartening" in a social media post and said the community is praying for her safe return.

Anyone with information is urged to contact the South Saint George Police Station at 444-4454, the Criminal Investigation Department at 440-3921, the police emergency line at 911, or the nearest police station, the Royal Grenada Police Force said.
Bonny Chu is a Breaking and Trending News Writer for Fox News Digital

title: Man faces murder charge after innocent 12-year-old is killed in Bronx street gunfire
summary: Surveillance video captures 12-year-old Jacob Freytes' final moments inside a Bronx bodega after a stray bullet struck him during a street confrontation.
story: Video shows William Ferrer being escorted by detectives after his arrest in the fatal Bronx shooting that killed 12-year-old Jacob Freytes and wounded two other men. Credit: WNYW

A man has been charged with murder after a 12-year-old boy was killed by a stray bullet while riding his bicycle in the Bronx, as newly released surveillance video captures the desperate moments after he was struck.

William Ferrer, 45, was arrested Sunday morning and charged with murder, two counts of attempted murder, manslaughter, six counts of assault and three counts of criminal possession of a weapon, the New York Police Department confirmed to Fox News Digital.

Police say Ferrer is accused of opening fire during a chaotic confrontation outside Wanda Deli Grocery on Elliot Place near the Grand Concourse in the Mount Eden neighborhood Saturday afternoon, killing 12-year-old Jacob Freytes, who investigators say was an innocent bystander.

According to police, Freytes had been riding his bicycle near the bodega when gunfire erupted shortly before 5 p.m. He was struck in the shoulder and rushed to NYC Health and Hospitals/Lincoln, where he was pronounced dead.
THREE CHILDREN SHOT NEAR PUBLIC POOL IN SMALL ARKANSAS TOWN, SUSPECT TAKEN INTO CUSTODY
William Ferrer faces murder and multiple other charges after police say he fatally shot 12-year-old Jacob Freytes during a Bronx street shooting. (WNYW)
NYPD Commissioner Jessica Tisch announced Ferrer's arrest Sunday, calling Freytes' death "an act of senseless gun violence."
SUSPECT ARRESTED AFTER ALLEGEDLY YELLING ‘ALLAHU AKBAR,' STABBING 2 MEN IN NYC ATTACK

"Jacob was an innocent bystander on his bike when he was taken from his family yesterday in an act of senseless gun violence," Tisch wrote on X. "No arrest can ever ease the pain of this unimaginable loss, but the NYPD will continue to do everything in our power to seek justice for Jacob."
Surveillance video shared by United Bodegas of America shows Jacob exiting the neighborhood bodega after buying a ball and getting on his bicycle.
WITNESSES RECOUNT 'SCARY' NYC STABBING AFTER SUSPECT ALLEGEDLY YELLED 'ALLAHU AKBAR' DURING ATTACKS
Police arrested William Ferrer on murder and other charges in the fatal shooting of 12-year-old Jacob Freytes, who investigators say was an innocent bystander struck by a stray bullet. (WNYW)
Moments later, as gunfire erupts, the video appears to show Freytes running back inside clutching his chest before collapsing to the floor as horrified customers look on.
The gunfire also wounded two other men. Police said a 34-year-old was shot in the foot, while a 25-year-old was struck in the buttocks. Both men were in stable condition.
Mayor Zohran Mamdani mourned Freytes' death in a statement posted to X following the shooting.

"My heart breaks for his family, friends and all those who loved him. Their loss is unimaginable," Mamdani wrote. "Our children should be able to ride their bikes on a nice summer day in their neighborhood without fear of being shot. We cannot accept this violence as normal."
The mayor also said he was praying for the recovery of the two surviving victims and thanked hospital staff and the NYPD "for their work to find those responsible for this heinous act."
New York City Public Advocate Jumaane Williams' office also mourned Freytes' death, saying "nothing could be more tragic."
"We mourn with 12-year-old Jacob Freytes' family," the Office of the Public Advocate wrote on social media. "Nothing could be more tragic: An innocent child on his bike, killed by a stray bullet."
The office added that "our children's safety is our collective responsibility" and called for "urgently implementing the strategies proven to make us safer."

Ferrer has had multiple prior run-ins with law enforcement dating back to 1999, according to the New York Post, which cited law enforcement sources. The outlet reported his record includes arrests on allegations of drug possession, drunken driving, possession of stolen property, menacing and criminal contempt.
Community members gathered outside the Bronx bodega where 12-year-old Jacob Freytes was fatally shot while riding his bicycle. (WNYW)

Fernando Mateo, spokesman for the United Bodegas of America, called Freytes' death a devastating reminder of the toll gun violence continues to take on New York City during a Sunday press conference outside the bodega where the shooting happened.
"We're just tired of having these press conferences speaking about gun violence," Mateo said. "Whether it's in a bodega, whether it is in a cab, it's gun violence on our streets."
Mateo said surveillance video shows Freytes entering the neighborhood bodega to buy a ball before walking outside moments before the shooting erupted.
"He runs back into the bodega because he lives in the area, and he's a regular in that bodega seeking refuge," Mateo said. "But no, he didn't make it. Twelve years old."

Mateo also said the store is equipped with one of the emergency panic buttons installed in many New York City bodegas, but the violence unfolded within seconds.

title: ICE prepares major operation targeting Haitians losing TPS after Supreme Court ruling
summary: Beginning as soon as this week, ICE plans to dramatically ramp up operations to find and arrest Haitian migrants in the U.S. who are set to lose their TPS, sources told Fox News.
story: Heritage Foundation immigration director Lora Ries discusses a Haitian national charged in the alleged killing of a Pennsylvania state trooper. Fox News correspondent CB Cotton reports on ‘Fox Report.’

U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) plans to dramatically ramp up operations to locate and arrest Haitian nationals whose Temporary Protected Status (TPS) is expected to end imminently, multiple federal sources told Fox News.
The expanded operation is expected to begin as soon as this week.

The Supreme Court’s certified judgment is expected to be transmitted to the lower courts Monday, clearing the way for the Trump administration to proceed with ending TPS for more than 300,000 Haitians.

Federal sources told Fox News that Ohio will be heavily targeted because Springfield, Ohio, has a large Haitian population. ICE leadership has been notified of the operational plans, the sources said.
SUPREME COURT'S LATEST IMMIGRATION RULING WILL CAUSE AMERICANS TO 'DIE AND SUFFER' ATTORNEY WARNS

A sweeping ICE enforcement operation targeting Haitian migrants who are set to imminently lose their Temporary Protected Status is expected to begin as soon as this week, Fox News has learned. (Charly Triballeau/AFP via Getty Images)
Last month, the Supreme Court reversed lower-court judgments that had postponed the administration’s TPS terminations for Haiti and Syria while litigation continued.

TPS was first granted to Haiti following the country's devastating 2010 earthquake. The designation allows eligible foreign nationals from countries experiencing armed conflict, natural disasters or other extraordinary conditions to temporarily live and work legally in the United States.
SUPREME COURT WEIGHS TRUMP EFFORT TO TERMINATE TEMPORARY PROTECTIONS FOR HAITIAN, SYRIAN MIGRANTS
The anticipated operation follows the Trump administration's ongoing efforts to end Haiti's TPS designation. (Jaque Silva/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

The anticipated enforcement operation follows the Trump administration's long-running effort to end Haiti's TPS designation, arguing that the program was never intended to become a permanent form of legal status.
Following the Supreme Court's decision, White House spokeswoman Abigail Jackson called the ruling "a tremendous win" for the administration.

"Today, the Supreme Court affirmed what President Trump has always maintained: temporary protected status is, by definition, temporary. It was never intended to be a pathway to permanent status or legal residency," Jackson told Fox News Digital. "The Trump Administration continues to lawfully end the egregious abuses to our immigration system that have hurt Americans for years."
Department of Homeland Security (DHS) General Counsel James Percival also praised the ruling in a post on X.
"The Court vindicates DHS yet again," Percival wrote. "The T in TPS stands for TEMPORARY, yet many of these designations became de facto amnesty. This is a win for the rule of law and common sense."
HOUSE REPUBLICANS MOVE TO MAKE TRUMP'S BORDER POLICIES PERMANENT

The anticipated enforcement operation comes as Springfield remains a focal point in the national immigration debate after the rapid growth of its Haitian community thrust the Ohio city into the national spotlight during the 2024 presidential campaign.

Fox News Digital's Alex Koch and Robert McGreevy contributed to this report.
Stepheny Price is a Writer at Fox News with a focus on West Coast and Midwest news, missing persons, national and international crime stories, homicide cases, and border security.

title: One dead, 6 injured after gunfire erupts at unsanctioned California party that drew hundreds: sheriff
summary: A massive rural California party turned deadly when gunfire broke out, leaving one person dead and six wounded as authorities launched a homicide investigation.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

At least one person was killed, and six others were injured after gunfire erupted at a massive party in rural California Saturday night, sending hundreds of attendees scrambling for safety, authorities said.
The incident unfolded shortly after 10 p.m. local time in Morgan Hill, about 25 miles south of San Jose, according to the Santa Clara County Sheriff's Office.
Authorities said the gathering was an unsanctioned party promoted on social media that drew more than 300 attendees.
GUNFIRE SHATTERS TORONTO LATIN STREET FESTIVAL, LEAVING AT LEAST 2 DEAD AND MULTIPLE WOUNDED
FILE - A shooting erupted in Morgan Hill, California, about 25 miles south of San Jose, on July 25, 2026, prompting San Jose police to respond to the scene. (KTVU)

Deputies initially responded to reports of intoxicated people in the road and someone throwing bottles at passing vehicles, but arrived to find the party in chaos after gunfire erupted, according to the sheriff's office.
Responding deputies provided lifesaving aid until emergency medical personnel arrived, but one person was pronounced dead at the scene.
Officials said multiple others suffered gunshot wounds and were rushed to local hospitals.
GUNMAN CHARGED AFTER WOUNDING 9 IN TUCSON NIGHTLIFE SHOOTING BEFORE COP TAKES HIM DOWN

FILE - The Anderson Lake is seen in unincorporated Morgan Hill, California, on Aug. 8, 2022. Authorities are investigating a deadly shooting at an unsanctioned Morgan Hill party that drew more than 300 attendees. (Li Jianguo/Xinhua)
Preliminary information indicates the suspect used a handgun, though no suspects have been publicly identified.
Homicide detectives said they believe the shooting was an isolated incident and noted the investigation is expected to be "lengthy and complex."

"This tragic and senseless violence is entirely unacceptable," Santa Clara County Sheriff Robert Jonsen said in a statement. "Our hearts go out to the victim's family, those recovering from their injuries and everyone in our community affected by this traumatic event."
"We will work tirelessly until those responsible for this horrific act are identified, apprehended, and held fully accountable," Jonsen added.

FILE - Multiple law enforcement agencies responded after a shooting erupted in Morgan Hill, California, on July 25, 2026, leaving one person dead and six others injured. (DAVID PASHAEE/Middle East Images/AFP)

title: TikTok influencer who accused estranged husband of pedophilia found dead in possible murder-suicide
summary: Sara Gilson filed a protective order against Jeremiah Shawn Duffey weeks before police found both dead from apparent gunshot wounds in their Owasso home.
story: A wealthy restaurateur is accused of killing his pregnant wife and their two children in a Texas murder-suicide. (KRIV)

TikTok influencer Sara Gilson, also known as Sara Duffey, posted weeks ago alleging that her husband was a pedophile. The estranged couple has since been found shot to death in the woman's Oklahoma home in what is reportedly believed to have been a murder-suicide.

Gilson, who had recently filed a protective order against her husband, 48-year-old Jeremiah "Shawn" Duffey, posted the TikTok video on July 11. It was captioned, "Preparing for when Netflix drops a documentary about my soon to be ex husband who I just found out is a pedophile." The video was still visible on her account as of Saturday.

Thirteen days after she posted that video, police reportedly responded to a domestic call on July 24 at 41-year-old Gilson's home. When officers arrived, they found Gilson and Duffey dead from apparent gunshot wounds, according to local outlet KTUL.
FORMER DEM VIRGINIA LT. GOV. KILLS WIFE, HIMSELF IN SHOCKING MURDER-SUICIDE: POLICE
Gilson had recently filed a protective order against Duffey and posted a video accusing him of sexual misconduct involving a minor. (TikTok/ @mrsgilson)

KTUL cited an extended family member who identified the pair as the dead bodies in the home and said that Jeremiah, who went by Shawn, allegedly broke into the home, killed Sara and then himself. Police confirmed the couple's identities, according to local outlet KRMG, but did not say if it was a murder-suicide.
Police insisted there was no threat to the public at this time, according to KRMG.
HOUSTON RESTAURATEUR SUSPECTED OF KILLING PREGNANT WIFE AND TWO CHILDREN BEFORE TAKING HIS OWN LIFE
Police found Sara Gilson and Jeremiah "Shawn" Duffey dead after responding to a domestic call at her home, according to local reports. (TikTok/ @mrsgilson; Ajax9, iStock via Getty Images)
Authorities also said that the 911 call came from a juvenile in the house, the local media outlets reported.
Duffey had been ordered to stay at least 100 yards away from Gilson as part of her June 10 protective order against him.

On the same day she filed her protective order, another woman filed for a separate protective order against Duffey after he was allegedly spotted "kissing and fondling" her 15-year-old daughter, who played on the youth basketball team Duffey coached, according to The Oklahoman.
TEACHER WHO SERVED AS GOP STATE LAWMAKER ALLEGEDLY USED ROBLOX TO LURE STUDENT INTO SEXUAL RELATIONSHIP
Duffey had allegedly been sending the girl inappropriate messages and had given her money "to keep her quiet," the outlet reported.
After the coach was allegedly spotted with the girl, a report had been filed to the Owasso Police Department.
Gilson posted a TikTok video, following the format of a popular trend, in which she alleged her estranged husband was a "pedophile." (TikTok/ @mrsgilson)

Gilson had also filed two previous protective orders against Duffey, though both were dismissed after Gilson failed to appear at the hearings, People reported.
Gilson and Duffey had reportedly shared children of their own.
Fox News Digital contacted the Owasso Police Department for confirmation and further details.

title: Missing Grand Canyon hiker, 83, rescued after getting separated from companion
summary: Gerald Guinn, 83, waved from steep terrain after a cellphone ping narrowed the search area, but rescuers faced a grueling overnight carry-out mission.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

An 83-year-old hiker who vanished in a remote stretch of Grand Canyon National Park after separating from his companion was found alive after an intense all-night search across rugged burn-scarred terrain, officials said Thursday.

Gerald Guinn, an experienced outdoorsman from Kanab, Utah, was found around 6:30 p.m. on Tuesday during a National Park Service helicopter search, about 2.5 miles from where he was last seen on the park's North Rim, according to the National Park Service and the Kane County Sheriff's Office.

Guinn disappeared Monday after he and his hiking companion intentionally split up while taking a short hike around 12:30 p.m. in search of a nearby historic object in a remote area near the park's northeastern boundary, the sheriff’s office said. While his hiking partner found the object, Guinn never showed up. After several hours of searching, the other hiker called for help.
SEARCH UNDERWAY FOR AUSTRALIAN WOMAN WHO VANISHED AFTER SENDING MESSAGE ABOUT GOING FOR A HIKE NEAR LAS VEGAS
The sheriff's office described Gerald Guinn, 83 as an experienced outdoorsman. (National Park Service)

Search crews from Grand Canyon National Park, Coconino County Search and Rescue , and Kane County Search and Rescue spent the night looking for Guinn. Teams searched on foot through burned forest, the sheriff’s office said, while drones, search dogs and helicopters helped cover the remote area.

On Tuesday, investigators were able to narrow the search after receiving a cellphone ping from Guinn's phone. When a National Park Service helicopter later spotted him, Guinn waved to the crew overhead, the sheriff's office said.
A rescue team hiked about 1.5 miles to reach Guinn after a helicopter spotted him in steep, rugged terrain. (Kane County Sheriff's Office)

The helicopter couldn't land because of the steep, rugged terrain, so a Kane County Search and Rescue team hiked about 1.5 miles to reach him. Deputies said Guinn was in good spirits but was cold and unable to walk. Rescuers gave him water and warm clothing while deciding how to get him out safely.
FIREFIGHTERS, POLICE PULL YOUNG WOMAN FROM SEWAGE-FILLED RAVINE AFTER DAYS TRAPPED IN 104-DEGREE HEAT

With darkness setting in, a helicopter rescue was no longer an option. Instead, a paramedic was flown to the scene, and about 20 rescuers took turns carrying Guinn through the rough terrain in a rescue stretcher, clearing fallen trees and marking hazards along the way until they reached a nearby road around 1:30 a.m. — a day and a half after Guinn first set out on the hike.
About 20 rescuers took turns carrying Guinn through the rough terrain in a rescue stretcher, clearing fallen trees and marking hazards along the way, authorities said. (Kane County Sheriff's Office)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Guinn was checked by emergency medical personnel and released, according to the sheriff's office.
The National Park Service thanked Coconino County Search and Rescue and Kane County Search and Rescue for helping bring the search to a successful end.

title: ‘Vibrant’ Florida grandma allegedly killed by illegal immigrant outside Publix, family fights for justice
summary: Carlos Suarez-Contreras, allegedly in the U.S. illegally from Venezuela, is charged after backing over Deborah Murphy, 82, in a Publix parking lot, police say.
story: Surveillance video shows the moments before Venezuelan national Carlos Suarez-Contreras allegedly backed his SUV into Deborah Murphy and killed her in the parking lot of a Publix store in Panama City, Florida. (Florida Highway Patrol)
A Venezuelan man allegedly in the United States illegally is in jail after being charged in the death of an elderly Florida woman by backing over her with an SUV in a grocery store parking lot.

On May 17, Deborah Murphy, an 82-year-old grandmother, was walking back to her car on a crosswalk outside a Publix in Panama City Beach when she was struck by a Toyota 4Runner, according to court records.
She was pushed to the ground by the SUV, but the vehicle continued backing up, "running over Ms. Murphy," according to an arrest affidavit submitted by the Florida Highway Patrol.
Deborah Murphy, 82, was killed in Florida on May 17, 2026. (Courtesy of Amy Edge)
ICE URGES NORTH CAROLINA TO KEEP ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT CHARGED IN TRIPLE-FATAL HIT-AND-RUN BEHIND BARS
Carlos Suarez-Contreras, 26, was the driver of the vehicle, court records show. Luis Sanabria, 29, was the front-seat passenger.
Both were determined to be in the country illegally, according to arrest records.
DOJ DEMANDS SANCTUARY STATES END 'BLATANTLY UNLAWFUL' ANTI-ICE POLICY AS A MATTER OF LIFE AND DEATH

Both men told deputies they were born in Venezuela. The two were issued U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) detainers and booked into the Bay County Sheriff’s Office Jail, court records show.

Suarez-Contreras submitted a written plea of not guilty to the charge of driving with a canceled license and causing a death, a third-degree felony. His Georgia license had been canceled, according to arrest records.
Carlos Suarez-Contreras was charged in Deborah Murphy's death. (Bay County Sheriff’s Office)
ILLEGAL TRUCKER CASES FUEL GOP PUSH TO CRACK DOWN ON CDL MILLS AS DEMS LARGELY SILENT

Under Florida law, an illegal immigrant cannot obtain a state-issued driver’s license. However, 19 states and the District of Columbia do issue licenses to "unauthorized residents," according to the National Conference of State Legislatures.
At the scene, Sanabria gave sworn testimony to law enforcement that Suarez-Contreras "was operating the vehicle at the time of the crash."
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE
Luis Sanabria, an illegal immigrant, was a passenger in the car when Deborah Murphy was killed outside a Publix in Panama City Beach, Florida, police said. (Bay County Sheriff’s Office)
Before conducting an immigration investigation, the deputy on the scene noted that Suarez-Contreras gave "suspicious" answers to his questions.
Sanabria immediately left the scene on foot before law enforcement arrived, according to arrest records. He "only returned when I had Suarez-Contreras call him," a deputy reported later.
SEND US A TIP

Sanabria was found to have an expired visa, according to the incident report. He was released into the custody of ICE, Jacob Navarro, public affairs specialist for the Bay County Sheriff’s Office, told Fox News Digital.
Suarez-Contreras is being held without bond because of his immigration status and because it is believed that "he is a potential flight risk," Florida Highway Patrol records show.
Shoppers use the crosswalk in front of a Publix supermarket in Alachua, Fla., on July 20, 2026. (Natasha Holt for Fox News Digital)
GOT A TIP?
Just after the incident, Murphy was taken to the hospital and died from injuries related to the crash, according to court documents.
Suarez-Contreras is scheduled to be arraigned on Aug. 17 at the Bay County Courthouse in Panama City, Florida.

"We’re determined to find justice and see Suarez-Contreras held accountable for his reckless actions," Murphy's twin daughters, Beth Schulz and Amy Edge, told Fox News Digital on a phone call. "She touched so many lives as an amazing friend, teacher, mother and grandmother."
Her family remembers her as "a light" who was "vibrant with so many more memories to be made."
Deborah Murphy with her husband, retired Air Force Col. George Murphy, and their grandchildren on a Florida beach. (Courtesy of Amy Edge)
Crashes injuring pedestrians

About 16% of fatal traffic crashes in the U.S. involved drivers with invalid licenses in 2024, according to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA). That same year, 7,080 pedestrians were killed in traffic crashes and more than 71,000 pedestrians were injured.

The state of Florida reported 10,501 pedestrian-related crashes in 2024, according to the Florida Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles. There were 678 deaths attributed to those incidents. Drivers failing to look behind them when backing a vehicle in a parking lot is listed as one of the most common reasons for pedestrian crashes by NHTSA.
The Georgia Department of Driver Services told Fox News Digital that Suarez-Contreras' license has been canceled. The agency would not say when it was canceled, citing privacy reasons.
The attorney defending Suarez-Contreras told Fox News Digital in an email that his client "didn’t commit any crime regarding the charges he was arrested on."
"It’s simply an unfortunate incident and not criminal in nature," wrote Russell Ramey of Musca Law in Panama City.

One of Murphy’s grandchildren presented the family with a collection of reflections on life from Murphy in her own words, her daughters said.

"My husband and I always felt that the best thing we could do for generations to come would be to leave this world with people who would make a difference," Murphy wrote in one of the reflections shared with Fox News Digital.
"It has been a delight to witness one’s own legacy. I thank my daughters for making our dream come true!!"

title: Beauty queen Lindsay Shiver’s attorney rips Bahamas dispute he says could sink alleged husband murder plot

story: Lindsay Shiver and her husband were in the midst of a messy divorce and custody battle during this incident. (Credit: Thomas County Sheriff's Office)

FIRST ON FOX: Accused of conspiring with her alleged Bahamian lover to hire a hitman to kill her ex-NFL player husband, Georgia mom and beauty queen Lindsay Shiver should be free from prosecution thanks to "legally fatal" problems with the evidence, one of her attorneys said.
Her U.S. attorney argues Bahamian prosecutors lack the jurisdiction to pursue murder-for-hire charges over alleged conduct that took place while Shiver was in the United States.
"Lindsay Shiver is not guilty of the crimes alleged against her by the Bahamian Director of Public Prosecutions (DPP). Period," attorney Craig Shirley told Fox News Digital in a statement.
ALABAMA MOTHER SENTENCED TO LIFE FOR HIRING HITMAN TO KILL HER CHILD'S FATHER OVER CUSTODY DISPUTE
Lindsay Shriver and her lover, Adrien Bethel, far left, are accused of plotting to kill her husband and the father of their three boys, Robert Shiver. (Daniel William McKnight/ Instagram)

Shirley said the indictment alleges Shiver was in the Bahamas on July 16, 2023, when the purported conspiracy occurred, but he maintains her defense has provided prosecutors and the court with evidence from multiple independent sources showing she was in the U.S. that day.
"The DPP must prove it. Meaning that, as a threshold requirement, the DPP is required to prove that Lindsay was in the Bahamas on July 16, 2023," Shirley said. "It cannot."
DAUGHTER OF MISSING AMERICAN WOMAN TOUCHES DOWN IN BAHAMAS, SLAMS STEPDAD AFTER HE FLED AMID INVESTIGATION

Shirley argued that the discrepancy is not only a factual dispute but a jurisdictional defect that prevents the Bahamian government from prosecuting Shiver under its own penal code.

"This is not a technicality; it is a legally fatal defect in the DPP’s evidence, its charges and its continued prosecution of Lindsay," he said.

Shirley said that he was "shocked and disappointed" that Bahamas authorities were continuing to pursue prosecution against Shiver, saying that they have the obligation to drop all charges.
"Lindsay should never have been subjected to a prosecution that the Bahamian government lacked the legal authority to bring," he said.

Shirley noted that he issued the statement independently and that neither Shiver nor her Bahamas-based attorney, Terrel Butler, had prior knowledge he was providing it. Butler declined to provide comment.
Lindsay Shiver, far right, wearing a hat that reads "Bad Influence" is accused of plotting to kill her husband, Robert Shiver. (Instagram)

Shiver, along with her lover, Adrien Bethel, and the alleged hitman, Faron Newbold Jr., were arrested in the Bahamas in July 2023. Shiver, along with Bethel and Newbold, is charged with conspiracy to commit murder under Bahamian law. They pleaded not guilty to all charges.

title: Mississippi teen accused of killing elderly couple was suspect in ‘many’ burglaries, car thefts: cops
summary: Deputies say Cordarius Hobbs was suspected in many home burglaries and car thefts before the Mississippi teen was charged with capital murder.
story: Internet searches from conman Brian Walshe and voicemails from his mother, Diana, take center stage in new Fox Nation special on the Ana Walshe murder case.

FIRST ON FOX: The Mississippi teen accused of killing an elderly couple in their home was no stranger to local deputies, who named him a suspect in "many" nearby burglaries and car thefts, according to an incident report obtained by Fox News Digital.

Billy Blair, 74, and his 71-year-old wife Virginia Carol Blair were allegedly killed by Cordarius Hobbs, 17, after he broke into their Mendenhall, Mississippi, home on June 3. Family members of the teen said during a preliminary hearing in July that Hobbs did work for the Blairs for things like cleaning around the house before the alleged shooting.
Fox News Digital obtained an incident report from the Simpson County Sheriff's Department, which alleged Hobbs is a "troubled juvenile" who is a suspect in various other crimes in the area.
MISSISSIPPI TEEN ACCUSED OF KILLING ELDERLY COUPLE HAD WORKED FOR THEM BEFORE SHOOTING: FAMILY
Billy Blair and Virginia Blair were killed on June 3. (Family Handout)

"... When we first arrived I and other Deputies and Investigators believe the suspect could be a troubled juvenile known to us as Cordarius Hobbs who is also suspected of many other home burglaries as well as auto theft in this immediate area," the incident report states.
Billy Newsome, Hobbs’ grandfather, said he believes his grandson was called to work on the day of the alleged shooting but believes he's innocent.

"My grandson used to work for the man, why you gone rob a man that you work for," Newsome said. "Why you gone stay there that long and you know the police out there, and then you gone wait until everybody gets there to run, it just ain’t adding up, something just ain’t right here."
MISSISSIPPI TEEN ACCUSED OF KILLING ELDERLY COUPLE HAD WORKED FOR THEM BEFORE SHOOTING: FAMILY
Cordarius Hobbs faces murder charges in addition to several more felonies. (Rankin County Jail)

The workers called the Simpson County Sheriff's Department for a welfare check at 11:30 a.m.

By noon, the investigator said that officers arrived and were met with shots fired at them, starting a nearly two-hour-long standoff. Hobbs was captured after trying to run away from officers, the official said, adding that the teen was unarmed when he was caught.

Vaughn argued after a court hearing that there's a lack of direct forensic evidence connecting the teenager to the shooting.

"There was nothing to say he’s a principal, he’s the one that pulled the trigger on these things," Vaughn said.
