“These claims are entirely untrue. This includes fabricated reports of past medical issues, as well as false narratives surrounding family relationships,” the statement continued. The family asked people to “not believe or share any information,” unless it comes directly from them or an “official family representative.”

While the Norris family didn’t specify which posts triggered their statement, one notable AI image that made the rounds depicted his funeral, attended by AI-generated versions of Sylvester Stallone, Arnold Schwarzenegger, Jackie Chan, Bruce Willis, Dolph Lundgren and Mel Gibson.

title: Do You Really Need to See ‘The Odyssey’ in IMAX? What 70mm and Other Formats Mean
summary: Christopher Nolan’s “The Odyssey” sparked a debate around its formats and the right way to view the movie. HEre’s what to know about IMAX, 70mm and more.
story: Christopher Nolan’s “The Odyssey” hit theaters July 17, and the struggle to secure IMAX tickets may be just as grueling as Odysseus’ 10-year journey across the Mediterranean and Aegean seas.
Nolan’s depiction of the Greek epic is the first feature film to be shot entirely on 70mm IMAX cameras.

Cinephiles will tell you this leads to an elevated viewing experience, but there is a supply-and-demand issue with finding screenings that support this special type of film. In an interview with Variety, IMAX CEO Richard Gelfond said 70mm IMAX theaters are sold out into the movie’s fifth week, including 2 a.m. and 7 a.m. screenings.
Casual moviegoers are wondering: What even is 70mm IMAX, and how much am I missing out if I can’t see it in the intended viewing format?
TODAY.com spoke to film industry experts to break down why watching “The Odyssey” has become an epic puzzle.
What, Exactly, Is 70mm IMAX?
70mm IMAX is a wide-resolution film allowing for a larger image quality than the typical 35mm film.
Film marketing professional Lia Baek says 70mm IMAX film “can deliver exceptionally high image detail and show more image vertically than most digital IMAX or standard screenings.”
While Nolan’s stylistic flair allows for an immersive, high-resolution viewing experience, there’s a catch: 70mm IMAX screenings are only available at 25 movie theaters in the U.S.

IMAX CEO Walter Gelfond told Variety the issue with making more IMAX 70mm theaters. “The problem is they haven’t made new IMAX film projectors in about 50 years. So we retrofit them, rebuild them and part of our strategy is to see how far we can take it. But certainly, demand-driven, I’d like to see more,” he said.

Walter Nicoletti, founder of Voce Spettacolo, a film production and distribution company, brings up the involved maintenance process and associated costs as a barrier as well. He says a single 70mm film strip requires a reel weighing over 500 pounds.
What’s the Difference Between 70mm IMAX and Regular IMAX?

70mm IMAX fills up even more of the screen than typical IMAX screenings, as demonstrated on the movie’s website. That’s because it presents films with a 1:43:1 aspect ratio, as opposed to regular IMAX’s 1:90:1.
“The IMAX experience can still be highly immersive, but it is not identical to an IMAX 70mm film presentation,” Baek explains.
There Are Other Formats to See ‘The Odyssey,’ Too
Aside from the intended 70mm IMAX experience and digital IMAX, there are still four other viewing formats viewers can choose from.
The film’s official website breaks down everything, including descriptions from the stars themselves.
Here are all of the options, explained:

“Each film frame has 15 perforations and runs horizontally through the projector. It is the largest and highest-resolution format available and gives you an unparalleled sense of immersion as the image fills IMAX’s signature floor-to-ceiling screen,” according to the website.
“When you’re in the theater, you’ll feel the full impact of how it was shot,” Matt Damon, who plays the titular Odysseus, explained.
Standard IMAX (1:90:1)
Standard IMAX (1:90:1)

“The film will be presented in IMAX’s 1.90:1 Expanded Aspect Ratio with select IMAX with Laser locations showing it in IMAX’S 1.43:1 Expanded Aspect Ratio. The film will fill your entire field of vision on the floor-to-ceiling screen,” the website says.

“The film was shot and designed to be experienced on the biggest screen possible, and IMAX delivers on this,” Anne Hathaway, who plays Penelope, explained in a video on the site. “It fills your entire field of vision, immersing you fully for the best cinematic experience.”

“70MM film is large format film that offers a bright, clear image up to 3 times the resolution of standard digital projection formats, with rich analog color by projecting light through celluloid. 70MM film has 5 perforations and runs vertically through the projector,” according to the website.
“There’s nothing like seeing a movie shot on film presented on film,” Lupita Nyong’o said in her video.
The website highlights this “classic film format” that “projects light through the entire 35 millimeter frame to deliver clear, high resolution images with rich analog color.”
In his video, Robert Pattinson, who plays Antinous, recommended this format for a “classic” experience exclusive to a movie theater atmosphere.
Dolby Vision
Dolby Vision
Zendaya called this format “an experience all its own.”
“Dolby’s dynamic range, brightness and color draws you in, giving you a vivid visual experience and what Christopher Nolan captured will be presented with impact.”
Premium Large Format
Premium Large Format
This format presents itself outside of the screen appearance in two ways: 4DX or D-BOX.
While both experiences involve vibrating seat movements, 4DX also includes corresponding weather and scent effects.
Tom Holland, who plays Telemachus, also highlighted the “wall-to-wall screens and superior projection technology.”
“If you want to feel the movie, see ‘The Odyssey’ in 4DX or D-Box,” Holland said.
Which Formats Do Film Experts Recommend?
Film professor Harry Marks shares his advice to anyone trying to decode each option.

“Nolan composed the film so nothing essential gets cropped across the other formats,” Marks says. “My honest guidance: see it on the best screen you can realistically get to, and don’t let the scarcity convince you that any other way is a failure.”
Standard digital screenings, such as 35mm and the Dolby and PLF, are “fully valid” according to Baek, but she says part of the image area is technically lost.
“They may not reproduce the complete image area, scale or physical film characteristics of the 70mm IMAX version,” she says.
Marks highlights that Dolby Vision offers extreme contrast and brightness, and, along with the PLF, they are by far the most available, and where most people will be able to see “The Odyssey.”
Why the Formats Have Started a Debate
There are a few aspects to the debate.
Online, people are pointing out that the movie looks different depending on the format you see it in — essentially, a portion of the image is cut off if you’re not seeing it in IMAX.
“Nolan did a disservice to the majority of viewers who don’t have access to IMAX,” one X user wrote, comparing images from two different showings.
Then, even if you can see it in IMAX, it’s hard to actually nab a ticket.
Experts say the debate and the demand shows that consumers are willing to see movies in theaters, despite at-home viewing rising during the pandemic.

“(Viewers are) willing to pay top dollar and travel long distances for an experience they can’t replicate on a OLED TV or smartphone,” Nicoletti says. “The format debate proves that people go to the theatre not just to see a plot, but they go for physical scale and amazing visual quality.”

title: ‘Love Island USA’ Star Nic Vansteenberghe Addresses Split from Olandria Carthen
summary: “Love Island USA” couple Olandria Carthen and Nic Vansteenberghe have broken up, Nic confirmed in a TikTok post.
story: “Love Island USA’s” Olandria Carthen and Nic Vansteenberghe — better known to their fans as Nicolandria — have called it quits.
Nic, 25, confirmed the news in a post to his TikTok subscribers July 26. The separation comes roughly a year after they were named runners-up last summer on Season 7 of the reality dating show.

“To Nicolandria community,” Nic wrote. “The rumors are true. I didn’t want to Give people false hope, so I wanted To clear the air. We will continue To love each other ALWAYS. It’s a sensitive, as well as a private Subject, thank you for respecting Our privacy.”

Olandria and Nic took a nontraditional path to one another on “Love Island USA.” The pair, whose season premiered June 3, 2025, were initially coupled up with other people; Olandria with Taylor Williams and Nic with Cierra Ortega. However, during the show’s infamous Casa Amor episode, the two were both dumped, only to be spared and coupled up together, allowing them both to return to the villa.

Sparks didn’t fly during their first coupling, and the two decided to pursue their initial connections. However, Cierra ended up being cut from the show due to controversy around her previous use of a racial slur. Olandria and Nic gave things another go, just days before the show’s finale, quickly becoming a favorite in the eyes of the show’s loyal fans.

Since leaving the island, both “Love Island USA” contestants experienced an uptick in fame, with the two appearing in a flurry of promotions together, including spots for swimwear, makeup and more. However, the two remained vague when it came to defining their relationship. While at the reunion in August 2025, the pair said they were taking things slow.

“I know people are expecting us to be labeled by now, and I also see comments like, ‘She better come pregnant and married to the reunion,’” Nic said. “We’ve always been believers in taking our time with things and not trying to let outside pressure dictate our relationship, and I mean, we’re going on trips together. We have future dates planned, knocking some things off the list ... Whatever she wants, I want to make sure it happens.”

As recently as June 2026, Olandria said that the two were still hanging out, but aimed to keep the details of their relationship private. She told Cosmopolitan that they go to dinner, watch movies together and have even taken a motorcycle ride with one another.

“We don’t monetize our relationship or put it on display. If you genuinely like spending quality time with somebody, it shouldn’t involve a camera every two seconds,” she told the magazine. “We enjoy each other’s presence and do what normal people do: go out, have fun, and get to know each other.”

title: Resurfaced Video Of Tom Holland’s Ballet Skills Has Left The Internet Stunned
summary: Tom Holland is set to portray legendary dancer Fred Astaire in an upcoming biopic. A resurfaced video in which he shows off his ballet skills proves why he’s perfect for the role.
story: Well, this should clear up any questions around actor Tom Holland’s dancing abilities.

Holland is set to portray legendary dancer Fred Astaire in an upcoming biopic. And because of the role, the 30-year-old has been the focus of conversation for some internet users who are unfamiliar with his strong dance background.

After one particular social media user on X recently questioned Holland’s ability to fill Astaire’s (dancing) shoes, others have been sharing an old clip of “The Odyssey” star absolutely tearing up the studio dance floor with his ballet moves.

“I think he’ll be ok!” wrote one user on X, who shared a 2017 clip of Holland, absolutely nailing some perfect turns on the floor of the Royal Ballet School in London. Unsurprisingly, the post went viral, drawing upwards of 161,000 likes.
In the clip, Holland completes a series of fouette turns with pretty impeccable control.
“The turns he’s doing here are so hard,” one social media user wrote on X. “The point is to make it look effortless but these are…so incredibly hard. I love this casting, honestly.”

The video actually comes from a seven-minute short film, produced by the London-based Flett Films, about Joel Kioko, a ballet dancer who grew up in a slum in Kuwinda, Kenya. Kioko, who was eventually able to secure a scholarship at the English National Ballet School, had the opportunity to dance with Holland while auditioning in London, according to the film’s description.
In the short film, Holland marveled at their shared appreciation for dance.

“It’s an amazing form of communication. You know, I’ve learned my dance moves in London,” Holland tells Kioko in the film. “You’ve learned your dance moves in Africa, but they’re the same dance moves.”

Holland, whose busy summer includes promoting films “The Odyssey” and the upcoming Marvel movie “Spider-Man: Brand New Day,” comes from a heavy dance background. In fact, he trained in ballet, tap and acrobatics for the titular role in the West End production of “Billy Elliot the Musical.” He was just 12 years old when he debuted as Billy Elliot.
His dance skills and physicality were among the reasons why Holland was given the role of Spider-Man, several who’ve worked on Marvel projects have said.
You’ve clearly got this, Tom!

title: Watch Prince Harry Surprise Meghan Markle During Her ‘MasterChef Australia’ Appearance
summary: Meghan Markle appeared on cooking reality show “MasterChef Australia” as a guest judge for the July 26 episode and received a surprise call from husband Prince Harry.
story: It’s the cutest thing!

Meghan Markle appeared on cooking reality show “MasterChef Australia” as a guest judge for the July 26 episode. And while the Duchess of Sussex’s presence on competition show had been a shock to the contestants, she got a little surprise of her own — a call from her husband Prince Harry.
“What’s going on?” Harry says cheekily, during the mid-episode video call. “Have I interrupted something?”
For the show, based on the original British “Masterchef,” amateur cooks face off for the chance to publish their own cookbook and $250,000 AUD, which comes out to roughly $174,500.00 in USD.

During the episode, four contestants were challenged to create a dish out of Meghan’s favorite seasonal ingredients, including Brussels sprouts, local Australian honey, quince, strawberries and more. The result was to be “fit for a duchess.”
Just as Meghan was tasting the dishes, she received the surprise ring from her beau.
“I wish you could try this,” said Meghan, who referred to her husband as “my love.” “These dishes are fantastic.”
The Duke of Sussex, of course, replied by asking to see the creations.

The former “Suits” actress is no stranger to the kitchen. In 2025, she starred in her own Netflix lifestyle show “With Love, Meghan.” In the show, which ran for two seasons, Meghan invited a slew of celebrity guests into her home to explore some kitchen and craft tips and tricks.

The “MasterChef Australia” was released right on the heels of some new photos that Meghan posted to social media of her recent vacation with Harry and their children, Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet.

In one of the photos, the family appears to pay a visit to Princess Diana’s childhood home. The snap features Harry and Archie carrying large bouquets. Lilibet trails behind them as they walk down a grassy yard. The location is believed to be taken at Althorp, the late royal’s family estate.

title: Ryan Coogler Reveals Actor Who Will Play The New Black Panther In Emotional Comic-Con Moment
summary: During a particularly moving moment at San Diego Comic-Con, director Ryan Coogler revealed that David Jonsson will take on the iconic role of Marvel’s Black Panther superhero.
story: During a particularly moving moment at San Diego Comic-Con,  director Ryan Coogler revealed the actor who will take on the iconic role of Marvel’s Black Panther superhero.
Speaking to a crowd of fans at San Diego Convention Center’s Hall H on July 25, Coogler announced that actor David Jonsson will take up the mantle, becoming the franchise’s new Black Panther.
The announcement comes almost six years after the death of Chadwick Boseman, the first to play the superhero in the franchise.

“The last time we were together, we got to make a movie. We introduced a character who was the son of a character that the great child and play our T’Challa in that film,” Coogler said of the 2022 film “Black Panther: Wakanda Forever.” “Today, want to tell you guys in this next film, he grows up, he comes of age.”
Coogler explained that the team spent time searching for an “incredible actor” to fill the role.
“I want you guys to give a warm welcome to our new Black Panther, Mr. David Jonsson,” Coogler said, before the crowd erupted with excitement.
A clearly moved Jonsson, who’s best known for his work in 2025’s “The Long Walk,” also addressed the crowd, expressing his gratitude for the role.
“Thank you to this amazing family that I have the honor and the privilege and the blessing to join,” he said. “Believe me, the honor is entirely mine.”

During the panel, Coogler was also confirmed as the director of “Black Panther 3.” And, along with actors Letitia Wright, who plays Shuri, and Winston Duke, who plays M’Baku, the group shared that the film is slated to hit theaters on December 15, 2028.

Jonsson will join the cast following years of Boseman’s critically acclaimed performances. Boseman made his first appearance as the character in 2016 film “Captain America: Civil War.” Roughly two years later, he became the lead in “Black Panther,” earning multiple awards and nominations for his stunning performance.

The film itself, Marvel’s first Black superhero movie, was seen as a major milestone that reflected the Black community’s cultural impact on cinema and beyond. Additionally it was a profound moment for Black representation in Hollywood.

Boseman died at 43 years old after a battle with colon cancer on August 28, 2020. The studio decided against recasting his role. Instead, the 2022 sequel revolved around the nation of Wakanda’s grief that followed their leader Black Panther’s own passing. It also served as a moving tribute to Boseman.

While the superhero’s sister Shuri takes up the mantle in the film, the sequel also introduces another successor at its conclusion— the son of T’Challa named Toussaint, who meaningfully shares the same Wakandan name as his father.

The Marvel presentation was a particularly eventful one. Along with the major “Black Panther 3” announcements, the studio revealed an upcoming “Ghost Rider” film starring Ryan Gosling. Marvel boss Kevin Feige also brought several stars from “Avengers: Doomsday,” which comes out in December, to the stage, including Robert Downey Jr., Chris Evans, Pedro Pascal, Paul Rudd, Anthony Mackie and Simu Liu, to name a few.

title: Ryan Gosling Officially Joins The Marvel Cinematic Universe As Ghost Rider
summary: Ryan Gosling was introduced on July 25 at San Diego Comic-Con as the star of Marvel’s upcoming film “Ghost Rider,” playing its titular character.
story: He’s actually not just Ken. He’s also a Marvel superhero.
Actor Ryan Gosling was introduced on July 25 at San Diego Comic-Con as the star of Marvel’s upcoming film “Ghost Rider,” playing its titular character, according to a press release about the event.
The reveal by Marvel boss Kevin Feige prompted the audience to erupt into cheers, giving Gosling a standing ovation.
“Wow. Is this really happening?” Gosling said in front of the sea of excited fans.

Gosling’s character has been best identified in pop culture for using a fiery motorbike as his signature mode of transportation. Considered an anti-hero, Ghost Rider’s main ability is his “Penance Stare,” in which he locks eyes with his victims and forces them to relive the consequences of their actions in the name of justice.
Writer and MTV News correspondent Josh Horowitz teed up the introduction by asking Feige a not-so-subtle question about Gosling.

“I feel like the fans really want to see Ryan Gosling as Ghost Rider. I just feel like I’ve seen all the fan art over the years, and I’ve been talking to you about it. I’ve been talking to Ryan,” Horowitz said during the Marvel Studios presentation at the San Diego Convention Center’s Hall H.

Horowitz continued: “Then I remember that time just a few years back — it was actually during Comic Con — I asked you about it. I asked you about the rumors, and it was so weird. The lights went out in the room.”
Feige cheekily responded to Horowitz, saying that “just because the lights go out does not mean it’s a sign.”
Of course, the lights in the room did exactly that before Gosling walked onto center stage.
“This is a character I’ve wanted to play for a very long time,” Gosling told the crowd. “So, Kevin, Josh Horowitz, Hall H — Thank you.”

“Deadpool & Wolverine” director Shawn Levy — whom Gosling worked with for the upcoming “Star Wars: Starfighter” film — will helm the movie, according to a press release about the panel. And Jonathan Tropper, who’s also on the “Star Wars” film, is writing the script, the release said. The movie is slated to hit theaters in 2028.
Speaking to press following the event, Feige said that Gosling was actually the one who pitched the concept.

“The truth is, Ryan talked to Sean about it. Ryan had an idea, had a vision, pitched it to Sean. Sean loved it,” Feige told Rotten Tomatoes of Gosling and Levy. “They came in and pitched it to us, and we loved it.”
The announcement follows years of chatter around Gosling’s potential involvement in the MCU. While on Horowitz’s podcast “Happy, Sad, Confused,” Gosling hinted at the Ghost Rider role.
“Some discussions have been had,” Gosling said in the March episode. “It’s a complicated situation.”

title: Watch Emeril Lagasse Find Out That He’s Become The Internet’s Latest Obsession
summary: Almost 20 years after his hit Food Network shows “Emeril Live” and “Essence of Emeril” went off the air, internet users are becoming obsessed with Emeril Lagasse.
story: Almost 20 years after his hit Food Network shows “Emeril Live” and “Essence of Emeril” went off the air, internet users are becoming obsessed with Emeril Lagasse. And he’s just gotten the heads up.

Lagasse, 66, shared a video on July 24 in which he finds out that old clips of his shows have been trending across social media. For weeks, the chef has been a hot topic of discussion as millennials and more relive their favorite, often-outrageous moments.
The chef, known for yelling, “BAM!” after hitting his dishes with flavor, is clearly reveling in the nostalgia.
“That’s some good s---,” Lagasse says in the video.

In the clip, Lagasse watches several of his iconic television moments from the height of his fame in the late 1990s and 2000s. There’s of course a snippet from an iconic Halloween episode where he cooks in full-costume, incredible crowd reactions, and a series of iconic “BAM”-filled moments.
Lagasse was one of the mainstays of the Food Network for about a decade. A master of Creole and Cajun cuisine, Lagasse racked up a following for his big personality and hilarious kitchen antics.

Though his most popular show “Emeril Live” came to an end on the Food Network by 2007, Lagasse never really left our television screens. He went on to host several other series including “Emeril’s Florida,” “Emeril Cooks” and more. He also makes frequent appearances on competition cooking show “Top Chef.”

In recent weeks, people have been resurfacing their favorite Lagasse clips. They’ve included one in which he gives into his well-known obsession with garlic, another in which he has the studio audience in absolute awe after he adds two beers to a dish and yet another hilarious one in which he reveals his hack for fixing an overly-thickened sauce.
Social media users haven’t been shy about the impact that the chef has had on their lives.
“I attribute my love of cooking to watching Emeril as a kid in the 90’s,” one person wrote.
Another individual shared that Lagasse “inspired me to become a chef.”
Truthfully, it’s no surprise that he’s been embraced by the internet. Sometimes, you really just have to kick it up a notch.

title: Beatriz Hatz Of ‘Love Island USA’ Wins A National Long Jump Title Weeks After Season 8 Finale
summary: Beatriz Hatz, who was a contestant on “Love Island USA” Season 8, won gold at the USA track and field outdoor national championships for the T64 women’s long jump competition.
story: Beatriz Hatz, who was a contestant on the most recent season of “Love Island USA,” may not have won the reality competition show, but she did just bring home a giant W.

The two-time paralympian, 25, won gold at the USA track and field outdoor national championships in New York City on July 23 for the T64 women’s long jump competition. The title comes just weeks after the show wrapped, with its finale on July 12.

The T64 long jump event is for athletes with movement that’s been “moderately affected” in either one lower leg or the absence of one or both legs below the knee, according to Lexi Global, a platform which explains the rules of para-sports.

While Beatriz started out in second place behind long jumper Taleah Williams, she hit her stride by the fifth round, posting a mark of 5.24 meters, according to ESPN. She secured the top spot after the sixth round with a mark of 5.11 meters.
What’s more, Hatz had some extra special fans in attendance. Season 8 cast mates Sean Reifel and Amora Robinson were there to cheer on their fellow islander.
“Shout out Bea,” Sean said in a video interview, following the event. “She’s a monster.”
Amora is also seen in the video, telling Beatriz after the competition, “We’re so proud of you!”

The results are particularly impressive given Beatriz’s inability to fully train while in the villa. Beatriz was among the original Season 8 cast members. She quickly made a name for herself for her blunt honesty with the other islanders and her jokes about her limb difference. Her time, however, was cut short. And by Episode 9, she left the villa after America voted to pair her then-partner Gabriel with new bombshell Jen Terry.
Beatriz told TODAY.com in a July 22 interview that it was impossible to keep up her usual regimen while on the island.

“My training will take three to four hours, maybe, on the track, depending on what we’re doing and how fast or slow we’re going about things,” she said. “But in the villa, it’s like, you’ve got time to do this, and then you got to go back to doing your other things, like having chats. So I had to be very efficient with the work I was doing.”
However, Beatriz said that she did what she could.
“I took my blade with me. I actually did some training with my blade on. I know they didn’t show it, but I was training,” she said.
Beatriz added that she “did a bunch of long jump drills, like repetitive takeoffs, a lot of technical work in the blade, and I did like a tendon ligament circuit, just as much stuff as I could do.”

title: Rick Moranis Gets Comic-Con Standing Ovation As He Comes Out Of Retirement For ‘Spaceballs 2’
summary: During a panel for the upcoming sequel to the 1987 “Star Wars” parody film “Spaceballs” at San Diego Comic-Con on Friday, Rick Moranis made a special appearance as Lord Dark Helmet.
story: Lord Dark Helmet is so back!

During a panel for the upcoming sequel to the 1987 “Star Wars” parody film “Spaceballs” at San Diego Comic-Con on Friday, Rick Moranis, who played the hilarious spoof on Darth Vader, made a special appearance.
The 73-year-old, who is reprising his role for the sequel, donned his iconic enormous helmet from the original film and walked through the packed house at Hall H of the San Diego Convention Center.
The crowd couldn’t help but give Moranis, who stepped back from appearing in films almost three decades ago, a standing ovation.

The sequel, entitled “Spaceballs: The New One,” is slated to hit theaters on April 23, 2027. The project was championed by several comedians and actors including Josh Gad. It will feature some familiar faces, like the original film’s director Mel Brooks, who is not only a producer on the sequel but also reprising his role as the beloved Yoda parody character Yogurt.

Moranis’ entrance was certainly a theatrical one. The actor did not begin the event with the rest of the panel. Rather, he surprised the crowd by popping up in the audience after being hidden under the helmet. The crowd, understandably, went wild.
Moranis, who then joined the panel, told fans about his decision to reenter the industry with the upcoming film.
“It just felt like this is it. It’s time,” he told the crowd. “I said yes, and it is the best decision I’ve ever made.”
The actor, whose reprisal of the beloved villain role was announced last year, also joked that he had never really left.  He said that he had discussed the idea of a sequel way back in 1989.
“I wasn’t really retired,” he joked. “I was just negotiating.”
The panel was filled with several other noteworthy moments, including a parody of the Marvel Cinematic Universe, the universe of Marvel superhero films that are typically released in “phases.”
For this event, the panel unveiled the “Spaceballs Cinematic Universe.” The MCU spoof included upwards of 11 phases including “The Almighty Schwartz Saga.” (IYKYK!)
Though Mel Brooks did not attend the event, he sent along a hilarious video message.

“Sorry I can’t be with you. I’m on the convention floor trying to buy a rare Charizard card. When I was your age, on a Friday, I would go to something called ‘work,’” he said in the video, according to Deadline. “From the bottom of my heart I want to say, thank you, nerds.”

title: Conan O’Brien Addresses His Shocking New Hair: ‘I’m One Of The Thunderbirds That Is Easily 55’
summary: Comedian Conan O’Brien, who’s known for his very red, very high pompadour, recently stepped out with a shockingly different hairstyle. And in a new video clip, he explained why.
story: Comedian Conan O’Brien, who’s known for his very red, very high pompadour, recently stepped out with a shockingly different hairstyle. And now viewers finally understand why.

O’Brien, 63, addressed the new look in a July 22 clip from his podcast “Conan O’Brien Needs A Friend.” Fans had first spotted the makeover during an episode of the podcast, which featured fellow comedian Molly Shannon, earlier that same week. It prompted many a question about the departure from his signature style.

The origin story, it turns out, begins at the June 18 opening of the Obama Presidential Center in Chicago, which O’Brien attended. The comedian explained on the clip that he originally did not realize that the event was outdoors. While he splashed a bit of sunblock on his face, the story would later take a turn.

“It’s three hours plus, and when it’s over, I’m so glad that I put the sunblock on, and I’m feeling really good about myself,” O’Brien said in the clip, joking that he felt superior to others like comedians David Letterman and Stephen Colbert, who did not appear to have prepared like he did. “I’m like, ‘Well, those suckers don’t know how to put sunblock on.’”
The good vibes did not last for long.

“A day or two later, after the event, I feel like my skull is on fire. And then two days after that, my skull is really itchy, and whenever I itch it, it looks like a snow globe,” he said. “White freckled confetti is pouring off of my head. It’s disgusting.”
It turns out that O’Brien suffered a pretty bad sunburn on his scalp.

“I talked to someone. They said, ‘Yeah, you got a sunburn on your scalp,’ which I’m not used to because I’ve got so much hair, but this sun just blasted right through my hair, and it roasted my scalp,” O’Brien explained. “To treat this, you’ve got to rub oil into it.”
The comedian admitted that while treating the burn, he had forgotten that he had podcast duties later that same day.
“Then I come in and I look like I’m in Sha Na Na. I’m a grease ball,” O’Brien said, referencing the doo-wop revival band.
Of course, he and his co-host Sona Movsesian and assistant David Hopping could not help but have a little fun with the new ‘do.
“I look like I want to fight one of you in the parking lot by swinging a chain at you in 1952, or a little switchblade,” O’Brien said.
O’Brien also joked that he looked like “one of the Thunderbirds that is easily 55 years old” in the 1978 film “Grease.”
Before he even addressed the hair, fans had been roasting O’Brien over the look.
“Seeing Conan’s hair like this feels illegal,” one social media user wrote.
Another person dubbed O’Brien “Coney Soprano,” a riff on “The Sopranos” mobster Tony Soprano.

title: Meghan Markle’s ‘Summer Holiday’ Snaps With Kids Include a Visit to Princess Diana’s Childhood Home
summary: Meghan Markle shared photos from her, Prince Harry and their kids summer vacation, which included time at the beach and Princess Diana’s family estate.
story: Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, has been soaking up the sun, enjoying the company of her family, and remembering loved ones this summer.
In a series of photos posted July 23 on Instagram, the former Meghan Markle shared a look at her recent vacation with husband Prince Harry and their children, Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet.
Among the snaps include a black-and-white photo of her and Harry laughing during a meal, Harry flipping Lilibet in the pool, Archie in the pilot seat of an airplane and Meghan with her pup.
However, there is one photo in particular that has captured people’s attention: the family visiting Princess Diana’s childhood home.
The photo shows Harry and Archie carrying large bouquets, with Lilibet behind them as they walk down a grassy yard. The location is believed to be taken at Althorp, the late royal’s family estate.

Located in Northamptonshire, England, the Spencer family 13,000 acre estate is where Princess Diana is buried on a secluded island in the Round Oval lake. While the estate is open to the public, the burial site is off-limits.

Princess Diana’s brother and Harry’s uncle, Charles Spencer, lives at Althorp, meaning the family could have spent time with him while at the estate. On the Althorp website, it notes that the establishment was closed July 10 and 11.

Earlier this month, Harry traveled to the U.K. for a series of public events, including promoting the 2027 Invictus Games. He was joined by Meghan and their kids, who did not make any public appearances.
The family, however, did reunite with King Charles III, marking the first time he had seen his grandchildren in four years.
Buckingham Palace confirmed to NBC News on July 10 that the king and Queen Camilla hosted Harry, Meghan, Archie and Lilibet at Highgrove House, their private residence in Gloucestershire, England.
The last time the children saw their grandfather was in 2022 when they attended Queen Elizabeth II’s Platinum Jubilee, celebrating her 70 years on the throne.
Another snap that is making people nostalgic is one where the former “Suits” star is wearing a black one-piece bathing suit and watching her family getting into the ocean.
The shot was reminiscent of Princess Diana’s previous beach vacations, with her wearing similar swimwear.

Over the years, Meghan has honored her late mother-in-law with her style choices. Some have been more meaningful, including wearing Princess Diana’s jewelry, including her butterfly earrings and bracelet.

Other times, Meghan’s past outfits have drawn comparisons to Harry’s mother’s looks. One instance was in 2020 when the former actor wore a green dress and fascinator, with people comparing it to Diana’s 1982 Trooping the Colour outfit.

title: The Best New Books of 2026, According to TODAY  Guests
summary: Here are the best new books of 2026 according to TODAY authors and contributors. The list includes romance, thrillers and romantasy.
story: If you’re looking for books to read, beyond the latest Read With Jenna picks, you’re in the right place. Throughout the year, authors stop by TODAY to share the books they’re reading and loving lately.

Here, you’ll find the books of 2026 that some of your favorite authors are enjoying. They’ve also including a few books that inspired buzzy screen adaptations, like “The Odyssey,” because it’s never too late to catch up.
The experts cited in this story include:

Harlan Coben, a thriller author whose adaptations are sweeping streaming platforms, and whose latest book is the memoir “Plot Twist”Julia Quinn of “Bridgerton” fameIsaac Fitzgerald, memoirist and author of “American Rambler”Yasmine Cheyenne, wellness expert and author of “The Comeback Era” John Searles, the former books editor at Cosmo and the author of “Single Girls”Brad Thor, author of thrillers set in the world of counterrorism including the latest “Choke Point”Emma Straub, a Read With Jenna author whose latest is “American Fantasy”Poet and author of children’s fiction Kwame Alexander, who also edited the poetry collection “This Is the Honey”
Harlan Coben, a thriller author whose adaptations are sweeping streaming platforms, and whose latest book is the memoir “Plot Twist”
Julia Quinn of “Bridgerton” fame
Isaac Fitzgerald, memoirist and author of “American Rambler”
Yasmine Cheyenne, wellness expert and author of “The Comeback Era”
John Searles, the former books editor at Cosmo and the author of “Single Girls”
Brad Thor, author of thrillers set in the world of counterrorism including the latest “Choke Point”
Emma Straub, a Read With Jenna author whose latest is “American Fantasy”
Poet and author of children’s fiction Kwame Alexander, who also edited the poetry collection “This Is the Honey”
Here are the books to try this year, ranging from romance to thriller and beyond.
July 2026
"The MASH Up" by Laurie Marie Meyers
A rom-com about a woman who wakes up on her 35th birthday and is trapped in a game she created as a teen.

What John Searles said: “For fans of ‘13 Going on 30’ comes Laura Marie Meyers’ sparkling and laugh-out-loud funny romantic comedy about a woman who wakes up the morning after her 35th birthday to find that she is trapped inside a game of MASH that she created in the 7th Grade. This hits the millennial sweet spot and is a fun read.”
"Dominion" by Jean Kwok
The first book apart of Kwok's new fantasy series.

What John Searles said: “‘Fourth Wing’ — by way of Chinese mythology — meets ‘The Hunger Games’ in a perilous world where a young woman with no memory and little magic may hold the key to uniting the Dominions and saving the mortal realm, the first in The Silk and Iron trilogy, from the New York Times bestselling author of Read With Jenna pick ‘Searching for Sylvie Lee’ and ‘Girl in Translation.’”
"Helpless" by Jessica Knoll
A woman who attends her college professor's funeral is kidnapped by her ex-boyfriend in this twisty thriller.

What John Searles said: “A successful Hollywood producer returns to her college alma mater and is reunited with her volatile, obsessive ex-boyfriend. What begins as an unsettling chance encounter spirals into a dark, twisty erotic thriller when Henry drugs and kidnaps her, forcing Faye to confront years-old secrets and the true, dangerous nature of their twisted past. Juicy and fun and full of twists.”
"The Odyssey" by Homer
The greek classic.

What John said: “It seems so surprising to me but the classic Greek poem we all had to study in college is being released as one of summer’s biggest movies, starring Anne Hathaway and Matt Damon and Tom Holland. Directed by Christopher Nolan, the film was shot entirely on IMAX cameras in breathtaking locations like Greece, Iceland and Italy. It stars Matt Damon as Odysseus, Anne Hathaway as Penelope, Tom Holland as Telemachus, and Zendaya as Athena.”
June 2026
"Phoebe Berman's Gonna Lose It" by Brooke Averick
A funny, warm story about a hopeless romantic determined to lose her virginity before her 30th birthday.

What Isaac Fitzgerald said: “‘Phoebe Berman’s Gonna Lose It’ is oh so warm and deeply charming — a novel about romance, friendship, anxiety, and the strange little deadlines we invent for becoming ourselves. In this case, well, losing one’s virginity before turning 30. Laugh-out-loud funny while still being tender and big-hearted, here is a love story in the truest sense, about learning to want honestly, messily and entirely on your own terms.”
"Main Characters: A Novel" by Bobby Palmer
A love story of a pair whose paths unexpectedly cross throughout two decades, told from outside perspectives.

What Isaac Fitzgerald said: “Main Characters’ is a brilliant book — a captivating love story told from the margins by the people who perhaps understand us before we understand ourselves. The book follows Clara and Seb across two decades as their lives brush up against one another’s, but is told from the perspective of everyone around them. A clever concept that totally works, here is a great summer read for anyone who has ever believed in the life-changing power of truly being seen.”
"This Vast Enterprise: A New History of Lewis & Clark" by Craig Fehrman
After years of research, this is an entertaining history of US history's two famous explorers.

What Isaac Fitzgerald said: “An incredible feat, Craig Fehrman’s ‘This Vast Enterprise’ is a wildly entertaining history of Lewis and Clark — the product of more than half a decade of rigorous and immensely impressive research — that never loses sight of the adventure at its center. Fehrman brings this legendary expedition thrillingly to life by turning our attention beyond Lewis and Clark themselves, revealing the oft-overlooked people and perspectives that made the journey possible. Expansive, compelling, and alive on every page, this is a perfect summer read for America’s 250th anniversary.”
"The Art of Loving You" by Natasha Bishop
The sequel to Bishop's "Only for the Week" of an intimate, spicy romance set during a bucket list road trip.

What Yasmine Cheyenne said: “Impossible to put down, this romance winds you through love, loss and the joy thats possible on the other side of change. If you love a plot that moves you as much as it inspires you, this is your pick!’
"Love by the Book: A Novel" by Jessica George
An honest story about the complications of adult friendships and new connections.

What Yasmine Cheyenne said: “A page-turner that puts words to what so many of us quietly feel about adult friendships — the growing pains, the unexpected shifts, and the beauty of who finds you in the in-between.”
"Waiting on a Friend: A Novel" by Natalie Adler
A story about friendship and community during a time of defiance and loss.

What Yasmine Cheyenne said: “A debut that somehow makes you feel more alive the deeper it pulls you into loss — an absolute love letter to a moment in history that still echoes today, with all the heart and humor to prove it.”
May 2026
"The Lost Book of Lancelot" by John Glynn

What Isaac Fitzgerald said: “This is a wildly entertaining retelling of the King Arthur myth, focusing on the life of Lancelot through a lense of queer exploration. Glynn does a fantastic job blending historical elements alongside adventure and fantasy. Filled with incredible world building, Glynn’s writing shines as he explores the Arthurian era with authority, and breathes new life into these long-known legends.”
"Famesick: A Memoir" by Lena Dunham

What Isaac Fitzgerald said: “’Famesick’ is the singular memoir from a singular voice — famously ‘a voice of a generation,’ as the line on her show ‘Girls’ goes — and polarizing figure in millennial culture, Lena Dunham. But you don’t have to be a GIRLS fan to enjoy this marvelous memoir. For starters, it’s rare to get a celebrity memoir this dishy and confessional, this genuinely shocking, sure. But also, you rarely if ever get them this well-written. You can feel how much care and craft went into this book, how much intelligence and skill, which is why it’s getting the response it’s getting, and why it is likely to stick around well past the news cycle.”
"Burnout Summer" by Jenna Ramirez

What Isaac Fitzgerald said: “’Burnout Summer’ follows the story of Camille Luna, a young woman who has just gotten out of a night in jail for some small crimes after losing her job and spiraling. Camille is picked up by an old friend, Danny, who whisks her off to his beachside hometown in Rhode Island, saving her for the summer from her flailing, corporate life in Washington DC. What ensues is an utterly spectacular will-they-or-won’t-they where the guy is delightfully straightforward and has his life together and the girl is the messy one. Ramirez’s sparkling writing makes the beach town come to life on the page — you can almost smell the sea salt in the air — a perfect blend of escapism and romance.”
April 2026
"Escape!" by Stephen Fishbach
Stephen Fishbach survived “Survivor” twice and wrote a novel inspired by his experiences. For Straub, a “Survivor” fan, this book is all a person could ask for.
“This is a novel about a reality TV program based on ‘Survivor.’ He’s a really smart, funny writer,” Emma Straub said.
"The Reservation" by Rebecca Kauffman

Emma Straub likens “Reservation” to “bingeing a whole season of ‘The Bear.’” It’s an “immersive novel” set over the course of one day at a small restaurant in a college town, she says. The headline news in the restaurant? John Grisham has made a reservation and everything needs to be perfect.
"The Fountain" by Casey Scieszka
Vera Van Valkenburgh has returned home for the first time in 128 years. After enjoying the fruits of the fountain of youth, Vera is tired and ready for a release.
“We need more contemporary novels with fantastical elements,” Emma Straub said. “This is a debut, smart and fun. Immortality in the Hudson Valley!”
"This Is Not About Us" by Allegra Goodman
Filled with humor, this is a story about growing old and the love that connects a family across generations.

How is it possible that an apple pie could cause a years-long rift between sisters? After Sylvia and Helen Rubinstein’s sister passes away, their relationship is in turmoil, enough so that a baked good could cause a major problem.
Coben calls this his “favorite novel of the year” so far.
"The Left And The Lucky" by Willy Vlautin
This text is an honest display of the power of friendship and how, in various ways, it can save our lives.

“The Left and the Lucky” is the latest from an author who is known for his portraits of contemporary American life. In this one, a young boy befriends his next-door neighbor, offering him an escape from his tumultuous family life.
Coben calls this book “gut-wrenching” and “compassionate,” with shades of John Steinbeck. There’s “dignity and integrity” in this working-class story, he says.
"Mad Mabel" by Sally Hepworth
Mad Mabel is a funny, inspiring, story of an underestimated woman about to prove everyone wrong.
At 15, Elsie Fitzpatrick became Australia’s youngest convicted murderer. Now 81, Elsie has left that behind her — until a young girl moves in across the road and unearths her past.
“Sally Hepworth is a huge star in Australia. This is the book that’s going to make her a huge star here,” Harlan Coben said on TODAY. He calls this book “funny, twisty and suspenseful.”
March 2026
"Imperfect Women" by Araminta Hall
This psychological thriller explores guilt, retribution, love and betrayal through three fascinating perspectives.

Nancy Hennessy is murdered and leaves behind a secret: The identity of a lover who nobody knew about. Not her husband. Not her friends. Not her daughter. The adaptation is soon to air on AppleTV+ starring Elisabeth Moss and Kerry Washington.
"Where the Wildflowers Grow" by Terah Shelton Harris
Be inspired by Terah Shelton Harris' newest story of survival and redemption.

“Where the Wildflowers Grow’ opens with a harrowing scene: A prison bus crashes over a ravine leaving only one survivor. Leigh survives and runs away to a flower farm in rural Alabama, starting a tale of hope and redemption.
"That's What Friends Are For" by Wade Rouse
Inspired by The Golden Girls, this hilarious story celebrates love, aging, and finding your people.

Fans of “The Golden Girls” will love this book inspired by the show about friendship and aging in style. Theodore Copeland’s estranged sister and her granddaughter show up at his oasis in Palm Springs, bringing secrets and disruption to his life with the “Golden Gays” (his nickname for his friend group).
"Python's Kiss: Stories" by Louise Erdrich
Explore Louise Erdrich’s writing with this magnificent collection of her stories.

Louise Erdrich, whose last book was chosen for Read With Jenna’s book club, has a new collection of short stories written from the past two decades of her storied career. According to the description from the publisher, the story collection features characters like “a tribal newsletter editor whose son tells her a story that nothing in her experience can encompass” and a girl who decides to spend her life with a stone.
February 2026
"And Now, Back to You" by B.K. Borison

What Julia Quinn said: “I’m not saying B.K. Borison has magic powers, but it’s a little suspicious that her romance novel about two meteorologists stranded together during the storm of the century is landing in bookstores right now... as half the country is clearing out from the storm of the century. Seriously though, ‘And Now, Back to You’ is simply delightful in every way. The characters are charming and real, and the book manages to make you laugh and tug on your heartstrings. Five stars, all the way.”
"Keeper of Lost Children" by Sadeqa Johnson

What Julia Quinn said: “I love when fiction introduces me to a piece of history I never knew about, and ‘Keeper of Lost Children’ does just that by shining a light on the true story of the ‘Brown Baby Plan,’ a 1950s movement spearheaded by African-American journalist Mabel Grammer to bring biracial children of white German women and Black American GIs to the United States for adoption.’ In Keeper of Lost Children,’ Mabel has been fictionalized as Ethel Gathers, who has moved to Germany with her husband, who is an officer in the US Army. She is shocked when she discovers hundreds of biracial babies living in German orphanages and, after adopting several children herself, begins a one-woman mission to find homes for the rest. I loved everything about this book, from the impeccably researched plot to the beautifully-drawn characters.”
"Project Hail Mary" by Andy Weir

What Julia Quinn said: “I loved ‘The Martian,’ both on page and screen, so it was a no brainer for me to pick this up. Andy Weir puts a lot of science in his science fiction, but he also spins a terrific story with compelling characters, including our protagonist, Ryland Grace, a middle school science teacher who is somehow tasked with saving the world from a climate fueled apocalypse. Fortunately for humanity, Ryland soon teams up with Rocky, an alien life-form who’s a bit like a metallic spider (but with a heart of gold and a keen sense of sarcasm). The stakes in this novel are sky high, but Weir keeps the story grounded with geeky humor, and it’s easy to see why ‘Project Hail Mary’ is predicted to be one of the biggest blockbuster movies of 2026.”
"How to Commit a Postcolonial Murder" by Nina McConigley

What Julia Quinn said: “Every now and then I pick up a book solely because I’m intrigued by the title. What is a postcolonial murder? And why do I want to know how to commit one? Georgie Ayyar Creel is a 12-year-old Indian-American child, who, along with her sister Agatha, are navigating girlhood in a very white Wyoming town where ‘Indian’ usually means Native American. Their lives are upended by the arrival of their uncle Vinny, who emigrates from India with his family. Vinny molests them, repeatedly, and the two girls decide to poison him slowly with antifreeze. I thought this books would be a mystery, and in some ways it is, but is much more a tale of girlhood, and sisterhood, and all the ways a family bond can fracture. Georgie’s narration is wry and sharp, often speaking directly to the reader, and in this way, we are forced to reckon with her choices as if they were our own. ‘How to Commit a Postcolonial Murder’ is the kind of book that is difficult to describe, but so very easy to recommend.”
Quinn also shared a list of books she read and enjoyed for the rest of the year:

What Brad Thor said: “Ten years after her best friend vanishes, a woman poses as a journalist to infiltrate the wealthy family connected to her disappearance. Every answer raises a worse question — was her friend a victim, or was she playing a deeper game?”
"Drive Me Crazy" by Lizzy Dent

What Brad Thor said: “Like an even steamier version of the Brad Pitt movie ‘F1.’ She’s an up-and-coming Formula 1 team principal. He’s her new hotshot driver — and her childhood crush — so their careers depend on working together without blowing up the team or each other. It’s high-speed romance with stakes you instantly get.”
"The Viper" by Brad Meltzer
What Brad Thor said: “A dying man hides something priceless inside the suit he plans to be buried in — then he’s murdered for it. It’s a killer premise with a personal gut-punch payoff!”
"People We Meet on Vacation" by Emily Henry

What Brad Thor said: “Best friends, polar opposites, years of summer trips — and the one question they’ve avoided: are they actually meant to be together? Read the book now, then watch the Netflix adaptation drop January 9. It’s your perfect ‘book first, binge next’ pick.”
"Mattering" by Jennifer Breheny Wallace

What Brad Thor said: “A lot of people don’t need another goal — they need to feel like they actually count. Mattering goes straight at the quiet stuff driving burnout and drift: feeling invisible, disconnected, and stuck on autopilot. Wallace lays out concrete ways to rebuild connection and purpose — so the New Year isn’t just a reset of your calendar, it’s a reset of your life.”

title: Darlene Love is Turning 85! Her Tips For Staying Forever Young
summary: Acclaimed soul singer and Christmas holiday icon Darlene Love has a gift for staying young. Here’s her longevity and health tips.
story: Acclaimed soul singer and Christmas holiday icon Darlene Love has a gift for staying young.

Love, who stopped by TODAY on July 24 to promote her upcoming documentary “Darlene Love: I Know Where I’ve Been,”  will be turning 85 years old on July 26. The songstress, who still continues to perform live, has opened up in the past about the many keys to her remarkably active lifestyle. But one of the most important secrets boils down to a particular mindset, she said on the show.
“You know what?” she told TODAY’s Al Roker, Dylan Dreyer and  Savannah Sellers. “I love life!”
Love also joked on the show that her youthfulness sometimes makes for awkward moments while out with family.
“I have a son who is 65,” Love said. “And they think they’re my boyfriends.”

The octogenarian has been lighting up the stage and screen for decades now. Born Darlene Wright, Love first got a taste of fame as a member of 1960s background vocals girl group The Blossoms. As part of the successful trio, Love sang with big acts like Elvis, Frank Sinatra, Dionne Warwick and many more. The three, which included Fanita James, and Jean King, even provided backing vocals to the Halloween hit “The Monster Mash.”

Love would go on to further make a name for herself with her 1963 classic “Christmas (Baby Please Come Home),” a track that is often in regular rotation around the holidays. Her extensive decadeslong body of work landed her a place in the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in 2011.

Love’s talents extended to the silver screen as well. She played main character Roger Murtaugh’s wife, Trish, in the “Lethal Weapon” film series. She’s also graced the Broadway stage as Motormouth Maybelle in “Hairspray.”

The soon-to-be-85-year-old doesn’t appear to be slowing down, either. And she’s been known for not only her electrifying performances, but also for doing them in 6-inch stilettos. For the multi-hyphenate, she’s said her youthfulness has to do with several factors, including a whole lot of rest.

“Sleep a minimum of six to eight hours. Your rest is very important because this profession is very grueling,” Love told the Digital Journal in a 2025 interview ahead of her Christmas tour later that year. “They say our 90-minute set is equivalent of a man working eight hours; that’s the amount of energy we expel,”
She also underscores the importance of staying active.

“You have to take care of your body, and I’ve always done that,” Love told the Digital Journal. “Right now, I’ll be 84 in a few weeks, I get up at 5 a.m. five days a week and I do a kickboxing class.”
Love also told the outlet that sometimes, she even walks the length of the Mario M. Cuomo Bridge in Rockland County, New York, where she lives.
“You really do have to keep yourself active,” she said. “Even when you are not working, you can’t just sit around and do nothing.”
Love has said in the past, she’s just thankful to be able to continue to do what she loves — performing.

“I thank God every day for my health, the fact that I still have my voice 🎤, I can walk, talk, and move like I’m in my 40s (okay, maybe 50s 😄)” Love wrote in a social media post in celebration of her 84th birthday. “Whether it’s good genes, pure luck, or just taking care of myself, I’m not questioning it. I’m just grateful 🙏🏽”

title: Didi Conn, 75, Re-Creates Her Frenchy Outfit for ‘Grease’ Show
summary: Didi Conn, who played Frenchy in the movie “Grease,” made an appearance at “Grease: The Immersive Movie Musical” in London.
story: One of Rydell High’s most famous students has returned to the school.
Didi Conn, who played Frenchy in the classic 1978 movie “Grease,” made an appearance at the July 23 London performance of “Grease: The Immersive Movie Musical.”
Conn, 75, wore a Pink Ladies jacket and fought back tears while wiping her eyes when “Beauty School Dropout” was sung during the show.
The actor also shared her wisdom on how to be a Pink Lady in a video posted on the show’s Instagram page.
“In order to be a Pink Lady, you gotta act cool, you gotta look cool, and you gotta be cool ‘til death do us part,” she said.
“And, think pink! Pink is the color of love. Just think about if you’re ever feeling lonely, there’s a big, warm, cozy, fuzzy pink blanket of love just hugging you,” she added.
Conn also met the show’s director, Matt Costain, and some of the stars, who asked her if she had any advice about being a Pink Lady.
“No, just love each other. That’s all. We really loved each other, except for Rizzo,” she joked, alluding to the tough leader of the group, played in the movie by Stockard Channing.
“I’m blown away by this,” she added. “All of you are perfect.”
Conn, who would later star on the sitcom “Benson” and the children’s series “Shining Time Station,” may have gotten a sign that the role of Frenchy was meant to be.

“My agent said, ‘You gotta go looking like the character,’” she said in a June 30 Instagram video about her audition for the part. “And all I knew was that her name was Frenchy. I did know that she wanted to be a beautician. And I’m driving home and what do I see, but Frenchy’s Beauty Parlor.”
Conn said she stopped into the shop and treated herself to a new hairdo.

“And Little Frenchy, she did my hair with at least two cans of spray,” she recalled. “I had a big hairdo and I learned so much about beauty school. And when I went to the audition, I told them the story about Frenchy. They told me later, as soon as I opened my mouth I had the role. I didn’t know that.”

title: Chris Anne Affleck, Civil Rights Organizer And Mother of Ben and Casey Affleck, Dies at 83
summary: Christopher Anne Affleck, mother of Ben and Casey Affleck, died in June after a monthslong battle with a terminal illness, according to her obituary.
story: Christopher Anne Affleck, mother of actors Ben and Casey Affleck, died in June after a monthslong battle with a terminal illness, the family announced July 23. She was 83.

Affleck, a civil rights organizer and teacher, received her diagnosis in December 2025 and was given six months to live, according to her obituary in The Boston Globe. She passed just after being able to witness one of her biggest ambitions, according to the family.

“Her greatest wish after her diagnosis, however, was to live to see her grandson graduate high school,” the family wrote in the obituary. “She did so, attending with her family on May 31, 2026. She died peacefully, in her sleep, two days later.”
Affleck, who was born in New York City in 1942, spent 35 years as a public school teacher in Massachusetts, the obituary said.
“Every student, whether just arrived from Haiti or Cambridge upper crust, was a cherished citizen of her classroom republic, equal to each other and to herself,” the family wrote in the tribute.

A Harvard graduate, Affleck also spent a large part of her life involved in civil rights movements. During Freedom Summer — a 1964 summer initiative aimed at raising awareness around violence against the Black community and increasing voter registration and political participation — Affleck got involved, teaching literacy classes, according to the obituary. An active participant in 1960s counterculture, Affleck also marched against the Vietnam War, the tribute said.
The family wrote in the obituary that Affleck’s unique, revolutionary spirit was present in her life since childhood.
“From the beginning of her life, Chris made her unconventional name her own, foreshadowing both the personality and the practicality that would follow her to her death,” the obituary said.

Affleck, the commemoration said, grew up idolizing her stepfather Sam, who was a World War II veteran and a civil rights supporter. During her years at all-girls private school Nightingale-Bamford, Affleck “made the most of an elite education while remaining skeptical of the tightly cloistered world it represented,” the obituary said.

In one particular instance, the obituary said, a teacher had chastised Affleck for her criticism of Jim Crow — the laws and policies that enforced racial segregation primarily from 1877 to the mid-1960s — without hearing the “other side.”

“She slipped down to a payphone to ask Woolworth’s whether they really did turn Black customers away,” the family wrote, referencing the now-defunct chain retail store. “That was Chris: always willing to acknowledge that she might be wrong and never letting that uncertainty be an excuse for inaction.”
She also had a sense of humor, proudly wearing a typo from her first email address that dubbed her “Chritopher” and embraced it twenty years, the obituary said.
Later on, it was Affleck’s five grandchildren — Indiana, 22, Violet, 20, Atticus, 18, Fin, 17, and Sam, 12 — that became the “animating force” in her life, the family said in the obituary.
“Chris was suitably proud of her descendants’ achievements, but she was delighted when they questioned, defied, or cleverly engaged authority,” the tribute said.

Affleck, who retired in 2008, remained involved in advocacy and organizing. She volunteered on the Barack Obama campaign trail, the obituary said. Shortly afterwards, she traveled to Palestine and, upon her return, became an organizer with the coalition group Alliance for Water Justice in Palestine, the family wrote. She was also a founding board member of the Sustainable Cape Project in Truro, Massachusetts.
“When her granddaughter’s student activist group needed a space for trainings, she invited them to Truro and attended every single workshop herself, taking notes,” the obituary said.
Even after her diagnosis, Affleck continued her social justice work, the commemoration pointed out.
“She called her friend, Josh Laub, to take oral histories of his time as a principal in the South Bronx,” the obituary said.

Ben Affleck has previously opened up about his love for his mother, sharing in an interview with Vanity Fair that he and friend and fellow actor Matt Damon were intent on bringing their beloved moms to their first Academy Awards experience in 1998. While Ben Affleck said that some felt the moment was quite unique, he told the outlet that bringing his loved one to the Oscars felt like a natural choice.

“We were sitting next to our moms and we won, and we kind of hugged our moms,” Affleck told the magazine. “And I remember, how everyone had made such a big thing out of it. As if this was such a novelty.”
“And I remember thinking, being insecure, like, ‘Why? Why is it weird that we’re bringing our moms?’” he continued. “Like, ‘Who else do you think we would bring?’ You know what I mean?”
Affleck added that there was “nobody else that was going to go.”
“That was it. Of course our moms were gonna go,” he said. “That really was innocent and not faked.”
CORRECTION (July 24, 2026, 10 a.m.): An earlier version of this article misstated that Christopher Anne Affleck died at 82 years old. She was 83.

title: Chloe Kim Has 1 Request For Fans Who Take Photos With Her — And People Say It’s ‘So Real’
summary: If you ever take a photo with Olympic snowboarder Chloe Kim, make sure you do this one thing.
story: If you ever take a photo with Olympic snowboarder Chloe Kim, make sure you do this one thing.
The gold medalist had a message to fans who post photos of them together, asking that if they edit themselves, consider touching up her appearance, as well.
“If you are going to stop me for a photo and you’re gonna post it,” she begins in a TikTok. “Facetune me too, ‘K.”
She jokingly continued, “Stop just Facetuning yourself, looking all gorgeous and I’m next to you like ... don’t. That’s rude.”
Many people in the comments section couldn’t help but agree with Kim, including fellow athletes.
Gold medalist and gymnast Suni Lee wrote, “pls this is so real.” Tennis superstar Coco Gauff also commented, “so real.”
“10000% agree,” wrote Olympic figure skater Adam Rippon.
Other fans loved her humor, writing, “I freaking love you you’re hilarious,” “Stop your so funny,” “this took me OUT omg.”
Some also posted previous photos that they had taken with her, with one person noting that they “didn’t have to facetune us bc we’re already fab.”
Kim replied, “omg.”
One person, however, brought up Abby Lee Miller’s post when she altered Neil Patrick Harris’ face in a selfie — and he took notice.

Back in December 2025, the former “Dance Moms” star posted an airbrushed photo of herself with Harris after seeing him, as well as James Corden and Bobby Cannavale, perform in the Broadway play “Art.”
Miller shared individual photos of herself with each star, but it was the snap with Harris that made headlines and caught the actor’s attention.
“Ummm… what did you do to my face..?” Harris commented on Miller’s post.
She replied to his comment, explaining that her past cancer diagnosis is why she edits her photos.
“Burkitt Lymophona, 10 rounds of invasive chemo & a big birthday — so I’m sticking with the filters!” Miller wrote. “You sir — always look fabulous no matter what!!!”

title: Some People, Including Keke Palmer, Are Just Finding Out Oprah Winfrey’s Real Name
summary: Keke Palmer was shocked to find out that Oprah wasn’t Oprah Winfrey’s real name. The media mogul then shared her name’s origin story.
story: Oprah Winfrey is one of the few celebrities whose first name is so iconic they go by a mononym. But it turns out that the former television host was actually given a different name at birth.

The 72-year-old journalist appeared as a guest on the July 21 episode of the “Baby, This Is Keke Palmer” podcast where she spoke about the start of her career and her success. Host Keke Palmer began the interview by sharing a fun fact she heard about the original spelling of Winfrey’s name.
Palmer revealed that Winfrey’s name is really “Orpah.”
Winfrey confirmed the fact and said, “It was Orpah from the Bible. Ruth, first chapter, 14th verse.”
She added that her name stems from the biblical story involving Ruth and Naomi.
“You know, Ruth said, ‘Wherever thy goest, I will go.’ And then Orpah said, ‘I’m going back. I’m sorry. I can’t. Too long. The road’s too long,’’ Winfrey playfully explained.
She recalled that she wasn’t the one who decided to adjust the spelling of her name and that the change happened following a mishap shortly after she was born.

“Nobody knew how to spell it,” she continued. “So, it turned out on my birth certificate, it’s Orpah. Then people started calling me Oprah. So it’s just the difference between the P being before the R or after the R. So once they started with Oprah, that’s it.”
Although the switch occurred when she was a child, Winfrey revealed she didn’t discover the truth about her name until decades later.
“I didn’t learn until I was, like, probably 20 or something that, ‘Oh, this isn’t really my name,’” she shared.
Winfrey told Palmer that the original spelling of her name remains on her birth certification.
The story about the origin of Winfrey’s name has resurfaced over the years.

During a November 2005 episode of “The Oprah Winfrey Show,” she introduced a clip from 1983 that showed her talking about her name while auditioning for a morning show in Chicago, according to E! News.
In the clip, Winfrey said, “My name is Oprah Winfrey. Oprah, spelled O-P-R-A-H, and if you notice, it’s Harpo spelled backwards.”

She added, “My folks did not really like Harpo Marx. We did not even have a television set for a number of years. Originally, I was named from the Bible by Aunt Ida, who named me from Ruth, the first chapter at the 14th verse, Orpah. But no one knew how to spell in my home, and that’s why I ended up being Oprah.”
The mogul has also responded to a few X users for over a decade with the correct spelling and inspiration behind her name.
When journalist Yashar Ali celebrated Winfrey’s 64th birthday on X in 2018, he included her real name in the tweet, surprising some social media users in the comments.
In 2024, one X user learned the spelling error for the first time and expressed their disbelief in a tweet. The post reached over one million views.

More learned the truth following Palmer’s podcast. Beneath a clip of the conversation between Winfrey and Palmer, one comment read, “Imagine changing your name because people couldn’t pronounce it, then becoming one of the most famous people in the world.”
Another said, “Orpah realizing she got the better stage name by accident is kind of incredible.”

title: Chelsea Handler’s Open Letter To Family’s ‘Lack Of Manners’ On Vacation Has The Internet Divided
summary: Chelsea Handler shared a list of vacation rules she has instituted among her nieces and nephews, which left the internet conflicted.
story: Chelsea Handler, who on July 22 shared a list of vacation rules she has instituted among her nieces and nephews, has the internet feeling conflicted about the pages of stipulations for going on holiday with the famous comedian.

Handler posted on social media the open letter to her loved ones, which was first printed in her 2025 collection of essays entitled “I’ll Have What She’s Having.” While some internet users said that Handler’s words were spot-on and a powerful message to all guests, others felt that the letter was a form of public shaming, that could only worsen any existing tensions within the family.
“It’s family vacation season, which means it’s time to reread the rules,” Handler wrote in the caption. “If you want to vacation with me, these are the rules.”

In the open letter, Handler shared several strict rules to which she called on her nieces and nephews — the children of Olga, likely referring to her sister-in-law, and sister Simone — to follow in order to vacation with her. The conditions included treating her employees with respect, refraining from over-consuming alcohol, cleaning up after themselves, staying off their phones during family time and treating their mothers with respect.

“Our family is dysfunctional, and that is what families are. What we need to work on, however, is manners,” Handler wrote in the open letter. “There was a definite shortfall of manners on this trip, and I left this trip feeling embarrassed and taken advantage of.”
In the letter, Handler also impressed on her eight nieces and nephews that they need to come to vacations “with an attitude of contribution — not one of taking.”

“I want you all to know that going away with me on these trips is not guaranteed. It is a choice I make and it is expensive,” Handler wrote. “A contribution does not mean financial. It means: What sort of pleasantness are you planning to bring on vacation? It is not a free-for-all.”
In the letter’s conclusion, Handler underscored that she loves her family members, but wants to “see you do better, and I promise to do better too.”

“I don’t need you to thank me all day. I need you to show respect to the situation and appreciate it,” Handler said. “I don’t care how much our family annoys you. It’s the only one we’ve got, and we are stuck together for life.”
Many social media users praised Handler’s rules along with her honesty toward her family members. In one comment, an Instagram user said, “sometimes you need to spell it out!”
Another person commented that they “agree with everything you said… maybe we need to plaster your letter all over the place all over the place.”
Several others volunteered to vacation with the star, joking that they would easily follow the set of conditions.
However, others were not as amused. Some felt it unnecessary to share the sentiments with the public.

“While I tremendously appreciate that you value and respect both your staff and your family, I’m not 100% sure you needed to call out your family publicly like that,” one social media user wrote. “It’s not wrong to call them out on that behavior — I would do the same. Exact. Thing. However, I don’t think they needed to be publicly called out in front of all your followers.”
Another Instagram user wrote that it’s “never a kind thing to shame people publicly.”
“This post was for you, to get acclaim from your fans. It was not something that was intended to make your family relations better,” the social media user wrote.
In her 2025 essay featuring the letter, Handler said while it wasn’t immediately embraced by her family members, it did bring them closer together.

Handler had taken a trip to Martha’s Vineyard with her family members during the COVID-19 era and was considering an additional trip to Maine. She decided to make the Maine trip adults-only, and she felt compelled to send her nieces and nephews a message based on the behavior she had previously observed, Handler wrote in her book.

“I’ve always wanted to show them how to be generous and kind, not only to the people they love, but to strangers. During our Vineyard vacation, I’d realized that they were acting in ways that didn’t meet these standards,” the comedian wrote. “I knew I had to address it, but I had to do it with love and grace instead of my old behavior of yelling, chastising, or threatening.”
She said her family was better for it in the long run.

“I was learning that just like my experience in therapy, change in a family dynamic doesn’t happen in an instant; it happens slowly and incrementally over time, until it sticks,” Hander wrote. “I had set a boundary with them, and while the initial reaction was shock, what grew out of it was a mutual respect and appreciation.”

title: The True Story of Dr. Tann, the Black Doctor Who Saved the Ingalls Family’s Lives in ‘Little House on the Prairie’
summary: Jocko Sims reflects on playing George Tann, the real Black doctor who saved the Ingalls’ family’s lives and whose legacy was revisited in Netflix’s “Little House on the Prairie.”
story: Laura Ingalls Wilder’s beloved “Little House on the Prairie” stories are back in Netflix’s new adaptation.

The eight-episode series, which premiered July 9, captures the prairie magic and hardship woven into a pioneer girl’s life on the American frontier. However, creator and showrunner Rebecca Sonnenshine said the series is drawn more from Wilder’s texts and documentation of frontier life than NBC’s original TV series, per her interview with the Los Angeles Times.
Among the most notable differences is the inclusion of a character whose real-life actions ensured the Ingalls survived to tell their stories.

Dr. George A. Tann (spelled “Tan” in the books), was a pioneering Black physician who served settlers, free Black families and members of the Osage and Cherokee Nations. He provided the quinine that saved Laura Ingalls Wilder, her father Charles, mother Caroline and sister Mary from malaria, which Wilder recounts in the “Fever ‘N’ Ague” chapter of the “Little House on the Prairie” book. The feature is the only time a Black person appears in the literary series.

“The reality is that there’d be no Laura Ingalls Wilder, there’d be no Little House on the Prairie, there would be no series” without Tann, says Susan Thurlow, an educator and member of the Laura Ingalls Wilder Legacy and Research Association. “He saved their lives.”
She also tells TODAY.com that Tann “deserves not only to be known as pivotal in their saga,” but also “an extremely important place in American Frontier history.”

Tann’s inclusion in the Netflix adaptation also challenges common perceptions of the frontier as an all-white space, Thurlow says. In southeast Kansas, the Ingalls lived on land that belonged to the Osage people, where indigenous communities and Black pioneers also shaped frontier history.

For Jocko Sims, who portrays Tann in the new series, bringing the physician to the screen is meaningful for the “brand new generation” encountering these stories of “community and working together” for perhaps the first time, he tells TODAY.com.
Read on to learn more about Tann’s real life, and what it was like for Sims to portray the historic figure onscreen for the first time.
Dr. Tann’s Real Story

Dr. George A. Tann was born in Pennsylvania 1835 into a free Black family of Afro-Caribbean descent, according to documents Thurlow reviewed. His status as a free man mattered enormously, as the majority of Black Americans were enslaved at the time.
His family’s property sprawled 75 acres, and Tann grew up working on the farm.
When he first left home, he made a living as a peddler in Danville, Pennsylvania, where he married his first wife and had a son.

Gaps in historical documentation make it difficult to pinpoint Tann’s educational background. There are no records of him receiving a formal education as a child, though it’s known that many Black children in the region were educated in homes or rented storefronts. There is also no documentation of him receiving formal medical training — which would have likely been denied to him due to his race — but he was known to have studied from mail ordered medical books. Most researchers also conclude that he likely received training as a physician’s apprentice during the Civil War, according to Thurlow.

Whatever route brought him into the profession, Tann went on to become one of the most trusted physicians in his region. In 1869, he moved to Kansas and purchased property in Osage territory, where he lived with his second wife about a mile north of the now-famous Ingalls family cabin.

He became the first doctor in the Cherokee Nation area, and opened a practice that ran a wide circuit, serving settlers and Indigenous communities alike. To those he treated, Tann was “very well known, liked, loved, respected,” Thurlow says. He was also rarely ever home, she adds, indicating the demand for his services across the frontier.

He practiced “eclectic medicine,” a popular approach that combined botanical remedies with physical therapy and other treatments, Thurlow explains. He was also a skilled surgeon who “pretty much had to do it all,” she says, although he specialized in obstetrics and geriatrics.
